title.zh: 卷三十四 列傳第四 羊祜 杜預
title.en: Volume 34 Biographies 4: Yang Hu; Du Yu
title.raw: 卷三十四 列傳第四 羊祜 杜預 Volume 34 Biographies 4: Yang Hu; Du Yu

sentences.zh: 羊祜 杜預

translations.literal: Yang Hu and Du Yu.
translations.idiomatic: The biographies are of Yang Hu and Du Yu.

translations.literal: A left angle bracket opens an editorial insertion in the received text.
translations.idiomatic: Here an editorial opening bracket appears in the chapter heading.

sentences.zh: （杜錫）〉

translations.literal: The gloss reads “(Du Xi)” and closes with a right angle bracket.
translations.idiomatic: The compiler’s note names Du Xi and ends the interpolated heading.

sentences.zh: 羊祜，字叔子，泰山南城人也。

translations.literal: Yang Hu, courtesy name Shuzi, was a man of Nancheng in Taishan.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hu, whose courtesy name was Shuzi, came from Nancheng in Taishan commandery.

sentences.zh: 世吏二千石，至祜九世，並以清德聞。

translations.literal: For generations they served as two-thousand-shi officials; down to Hu’s generation it was nine generations, and all were famed for pure conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Nine generations of his forebears had held rank at two thousand piculs, and the whole line was known for spotless reputation.

sentences.zh: 祖續，仕漢南陽太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xu served the Han as Grand Administrator of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yang Xu had been grand administrator of Nanyang under the Han.

sentences.zh: 父道，上党太守。

translations.literal: His father Dao was Grand Administrator of Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yang Dao served as grand administrator of Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 祜，蔡邕外孫，景獻皇后同產弟。

translations.literal: Hu was the maternal grandson of Cai Yong and the full younger brother by the same parents as Empress Jingxian.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hu was Cai Yong’s grandson on the distaff side and the uterine younger brother of Empress Jingxian.

sentences.zh: 祜年十二喪父，孝思過禮，事叔父耽甚謹。

translations.literal: At age twelve Hu lost his father; his filial thoughts exceeded the rites, and he served his uncle Dan with extreme care.
translations.idiomatic: When he was twelve his father died; he mourned with a grief beyond what ritual required and waited on his uncle Dan with scrupulous deference.

sentences.zh: 嘗游汶水之濱，遇父老謂之曰：「孺子有好相，年未六十，必建大功於天下。

translations.literal: Once he wandered along the bank of the Wen River and met an old man who said to him, “Young sir, you have noble features; before you are sixty you will surely establish great merit under Heaven.”
translations.idiomatic: Walking once beside the Wen, he met an old man who told him, “You have the bearing of a man who will win great fame in the realm before his sixtieth year.”

sentences.zh: 」既而去，莫知所在。

translations.literal: ” Immediately afterward the man left, and none knew where he went.
translations.idiomatic: With that the stranger vanished, and no one ever learned where he had gone.

sentences.zh: 及長，博學能屬文，身長七尺三寸，美鬚眉，善談論。

translations.literal: When he grew up, he was broadly learned and able to compose texts; he stood seven chi three cun in height, had handsome beard and brows, and was skilled in discourse.
translations.idiomatic: As an adult he was widely read and a capable writer, stood seven feet three inches tall, wore a fine beard and brows, and spoke with uncommon ease.

sentences.zh: 郡將夏侯威異之，以兄霸之子妻之。

translations.literal: The commandery commander Xiahou Wei thought him extraordinary and gave him his elder brother Ba’s daughter as wife.
translations.idiomatic: The local commander Xiahou Wei, impressed by him, married him to a daughter of Xiahou Ba.

sentences.zh: 舉上計吏，州四辟從事、秀才，五府交命，皆不就。

translations.literal: He was recommended as chief clerk for the annual accounting; the province summoned him four times as adjutant or as cultivated talent; five offices sent overlapping appointments; he accepted none.
translations.idiomatic: He was nominated chief clerk for the capital accounts, summoned four times by the province for staff posts and as “flourishing talent,” and courted by five high offices—yet he refused every call.

sentences.zh: 太原郭奕見之曰：「此今日之顏子也。

translations.literal: Taiyuan Guo Yi, seeing him, said, “This is today’s Yan Hui.”
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yi of Taiyuan exclaimed on meeting him, “He is the Yan Hui of our age.”

sentences.zh: 」與王沈俱被曹爽辟。

translations.literal: ” Together with Wang Shen he was summoned by Cao Shuang.
translations.idiomatic: He and Wang Shen were both recruited into Cao Shuang’s service.

sentences.zh: 沈勸就征，祜曰：「委質事人，復何容易。

translations.literal: Shen urged him to answer the summons; Hu said, “Having pledged one’s person to serve another, how can turning back be easy?”
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shen urged him to take the post; Yang Hu answered, “Once you bind yourself to a lord, leaving his service is never a light matter.”

sentences.zh: 」及爽敗，沈以故吏免，因謂祜曰：「常識卿前語。

translations.literal: ” When Shuang fell, Shen as former subordinate was dismissed, and therefore said to Hu, “I always recognized your earlier words.”
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Shuang fell, Wang Shen was cashiered as a former retainer and said, “Your warning has proved true.”

sentences.zh: 」祜曰：「此非始慮所及。

translations.literal: Hu said, “This was not what forethought at the outset could reach.”
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hu replied, “That outcome lay outside anything I could have foreseen.”

sentences.zh: 」其先識不伐如此。

translations.literal: ” His foresight without boasting himself was like this.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his prescience—and his reluctance to boast of it.

sentences.zh: 夏侯霸之降蜀也，姻親多告絕，祜獨安其室，恩禮有加焉。

translations.literal: When Xiahou Ba defected to Shu, many marriage kin announced severance of ties; Hu alone settled his household and increased grace and courtesy toward them.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiahou Ba fled to Shu, most relatives cut ties with his family; Yang Hu alone kept his household calm and treated them with added kindness.

sentences.zh: 尋遭母憂，長兄發又卒，毀慕寢頓十餘年，以道素自居，恂恂若儒者。

translations.literal: Soon he met his mother’s bereavement; his eldest brother Fa also died; for more than ten years he was broken and worn with grief, holding himself to plain moral conduct, deferential as a scholar.
translations.idiomatic: He then lost his mother, and his elder brother Fa died as well; for over a decade he was crushed by mourning, lived plainly, and carried himself with the modesty of a classicist.

sentences.zh: 文帝為大將軍，辟祜，未就，公車徵拜中書侍郎，俄遷給事中、黃門郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen was Grand General, he summoned Hu; Hu did not go. The imperial coach summoned him and appointed him Palace Attendant of the Secretariat; soon he was promoted to Palace Attendant and Gentlemen-of-the-Household.
translations.idiomatic: While Sima Zhao held the title of grand general, Yang Hu declined appointment; an imperial coach then summoned him as palace attendant of the Secretariat, and he was soon raised to palace attendant and gentleman at the yellow gates.

sentences.zh: 時高貴鄉公好屬文，在位者多獻詩賦，汝南和逌以忤意見斥，祜在其間，不得而親疏，有識尚焉。

translations.literal: At that time the Duke of Gaoguixiang was fond of composing literary pieces; many in office presented poems and rhapsodies; Runan He You for offending intention was rebuked; Hu stood among them and could not be drawn either close or distant; thoughtful men admired this.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Mao loved to write; courtiers showered him with verse. He You of Runan was cast aside for displeasing him, while Yang Hu kept a careful neutrality that men of judgment respected.

sentences.zh: 陳留王立，賜爵關中侯，邑百戶。

translations.literal: When the King of Chenliu was enthroned, he was enfeoffed with noble rank Marquis Within the Pass, one hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Huan acceded as king of Chenliu, Yang Hu received the rank of marquis within the passes with a fief of one hundred households.

sentences.zh: 以少帝不願為侍臣，求出補吏，徙秘書監。

translations.literal: Because the young emperor was unwilling to be a palace attendant, he requested assignment outside as an official and was transferred to Palace Secretary Supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: Unwilling to serve as an inner-court attendant to the young emperor, he asked for a provincial post and was moved to supervisor of the palace library secretariat.

sentences.zh: 及五等建，封钜平子，邑六百戶。

translations.literal: When the five ranks were established, he was enfeoffed as baron of Juping, six hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When the five-grade nobility was instituted, he was made baron of Juping with six hundred taxable households.

sentences.zh: 鐘會有寵而忌，祜亦憚之。

translations.literal: Zhong Hui enjoyed favor but was jealous; Hu also feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui was powerful, suspicious, and dangerous; Yang Hu was wary of him as well.

sentences.zh: 及會誅，拜相國從事中郎，與荀勖共掌機密。

translations.literal: When Hui was executed, he was appointed Vice Director in the Suite of the Minister of State and together with Xun Xu held the secrets of state machinery.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhong Hui’s execution he became a vice director in the minister of state’s bureau and, with Xun Xu, managed confidential state business.

sentences.zh: 遷中領軍，悉統宿衛，入直殿中，執兵之耍，事兼內外。

translations.literal: Promoted to Central Army Commander-in-chief, he entirely commanded the night guards, entered service in the palace halls, held the critical charge of arms, and his duties spanned inner and outer.
translations.idiomatic: As central army commander he took charge of all palace guards, attended the throne in the halls, held the levers of armed force, and bore responsibility both at court and in the field.

sentences.zh: 武帝受禪，以佐命之勳，進號中軍將軍，加散騎常侍，改封郡公，邑三千戶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu accepted the abdication, for merit as supporter of the mandate he was advanced in title to Central Army General-in-chief, added Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, his fief changed to commandery duke, three thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Yan took the throne, Yang Hu was promoted to central army general for his founding service, given the concurrent title of cavalier attendant-in-ordinary, raised to commandery duke, and granted three thousand households.

sentences.zh: 固讓封不受，乃進本爵為侯，置郎中令，備九官之職，加夫人印綬。

translations.literal: He firmly declined the fief and would not accept; then his original noble rank was advanced to marquis, a Supervisor of the Household of the Heir Apparent was established, the offices of the nine ministers were fully provided, and seals and ribbons for his wife were added.
translations.idiomatic: He steadfastly refused the ducal patent, so his old rank was raised to marquis instead, with an overseer of the heir apparent’s household, the full complement of nine high offices, and formal seals for his wife.

sentences.zh: 泰始初，詔曰：「夫總齊機衡，允厘六職，朝政之本也。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taishi, an edict said, “Now to oversee and align the pivots of governance and truly administer the six offices is the root of court government.”
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taishi era an edict declared that to harmonize the machinery of government and set the six ministries in good order was the foundation of the court.

sentences.zh: 祜執德清劭，忠亮純茂，經緯文武，謇謇正直，雖處腹心之任，而不總樞機之重，非垂拱無為委任責成之意也。

translations.literal: Hu upholds virtue pure and eminent, is loyal, bright, and honest in full measure, arrays civil and military, is upright and direct; though he holds a role at the heart, he does not gather the heavy weight of the central pivot—this is not the meaning of draping the arms in non-action and delegating responsibility to those charged with results.”
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hu’s character is lucid and weighty, his loyalty plain, his talents span civil and military affairs, and his integrity is outspoken; yet though he stands at the emperor’s side he does not hold the chief levers of power—hardly the model of ruling by trust and leaving execution to able ministers.”

sentences.zh: 其以祜為尚書右僕射、衛將軍，給本營兵。

translations.literal: Let Hu be made Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, right deputy, General Who Guards the Army, with the original camp troops granted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Appoint him right vice director of the secretariat, general who guards the army, and leave him his original camp command.

sentences.zh: 」時王佑、賈充、裴秀皆前朝名望，祜每讓，不處其右。

translations.literal: ” At the time Wang You, Jia Chong, and Pei Xiu were all famed figures of the previous court; Hu always yielded and did not rate himself above them.
translations.idiomatic: Wang You, Jia Chong, and Pei Xiu were luminaries of the old Wei administration; Yang Hu habitually deferred to them and never ranked himself their superior.

sentences.zh: 帝將有滅吳之志，以祜為都督荊州諸軍事、假節，散騎常侍、衛將軍如故。

translations.literal: The emperor was set on the will to destroy Wu; he made Hu area commander over all military affairs of Jingzhou, with plenipotentiary credentials; Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and General Who Guards the Army remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Determined to conquer Wu, the emperor named him military commander of all Jingzhou forces with credential staff; he kept his old titles of cavalier attendant-in-ordinary and general who guards the army.

sentences.zh: 祜率營兵出鎮南夏，開設庠序，綏懷遠近，甚得江漢之心。

translations.literal: Hu led camp troops forth to garrison southern summer, opened schools, soothed far and near, and won the heart of the Jiang and Han regions deeply.
translations.idiomatic: He marched his troops to the southern frontier, founded schools, and won the trust of both nearby settlers and distant peoples along the Han and Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 與吳人開布大信，降者欲去皆聽之。

translations.literal: With the people of Wu he spread broad good faith; those who surrendered and wished to leave were all permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He dealt with the Wu population in open good faith and let defectors go home if they wished.

sentences.zh: 時長吏喪官，後人惡之，多毀壞舊府，祜以死生有命，非由居室，書下征鎮，普加禁斷。

translations.literal: At the time when long administrators died in office, successors detested it and often destroyed the old yamen; Hu held that life and death had their allotted fate, not because of dwellings; he wrote orders to field commands and universally forbade it.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrates who followed dead predecessors often demolished their offices out of superstition; Yang Hu argued that life and death were fated, not fixed by buildings, and issued orders up and down the front forbidding the practice.

sentences.zh: 吳石城守去襄陽七百餘里，每為邊害，祜患之，竟以詭計令吳罷守。

translations.literal: The Wu garrison of Stone City lay over seven hundred li from Xiangyang and constantly harmed the border; Hu worried over it and finally by a stratagem made Wu abandon its guard.
translations.idiomatic: Wu’s garrison at Stone City, more than seven hundred li from Xiangyang, was a standing menace; Yang Hu worried at it until a ruse persuaded Wu to withdraw the garrison.

sentences.zh: 於是戍邏減半，分以墾田八百餘頃，大獲其利。

translations.literal: Thereupon patrol defenses were halved, and the surplus was used to open fields of more than eight hundred qing, with great profit harvested.
translations.idiomatic: Patrols were cut by half and the saved labor opened more than eight hundred qing of farmland to great profit.

sentences.zh: 祜之始至也，軍無百日之糧，及至季年，有十年之積。

translations.literal: When Hu first arrived, the army had not a hundred days’ grain; by his final year there was a ten-year store.
translations.idiomatic: On his arrival the army lacked a hundred days’ provisions; by his last year the granaries held a decade’s supply.

sentences.zh: 詔罷江北都督，置南中郎將，以所統諸軍在漢東江夏者皆以益祜。

translations.literal: An edict abolished the north-of-the-River area command and set up South General of the Household; all armies under his command east of Han and in Jiangxia were added to Hu.
translations.idiomatic: The court abolished the commander north of the river, created a south household general, and folded the Han’eastern and Jiangxia units into Yang Hu’s command.

sentences.zh: 在軍常輕裘緩帶，身不被甲，鈴閤之下，侍衛者不過十數人，而頗以畋漁廢政。

translations.literal: In the army he constantly wore light furs and loose belts, did not don armor on his person; under the watchtower his attendants numbered no more than ten-odd, yet he often neglected government with hunting and fishing.
translations.idiomatic: In camp he dressed lightly, went unarmored, and kept fewer than a dozen guards at his headquarters, while hunting and fishing sometimes drew him from paperwork.

sentences.zh: 嘗欲夜出，軍司徐胤執棨當營門曰：「將軍都督萬里，安可輕脫！

translations.literal: Once he wished to go out by night; Army Director Xu Yin grasped a staff and blocked the camp gate, saying, “The general commands ten thousand li—how can you lightly slip away!”
translations.idiomatic: One night he tried to leave camp; the army director Xu Yin barred the gate with a halberd and said, “You command the whole frontier—how dare you wander off on a whim?”

sentences.zh: 將軍之安危，亦國家之安危也。

translations.literal: “The general’s safety and danger is also the state’s safety and danger.”
translations.idiomatic: “Your safety is the empire’s safety.”

sentences.zh: 胤今日若死，此門乃開耳。

translations.literal: “If Yin dies today, only then will this gate be opened.”
translations.idiomatic: “This gate opens when you step over my dead body.”

sentences.zh: 」祜改容謝之，此後稀出矣。

translations.literal: ” Hu changed countenance and apologized; thereafter he rarely went out.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hu flushed, apologized, and seldom went out alone after that.

sentences.zh: 後加車騎將軍，開府如三司之儀。

translations.literal: Later he was added chariot-and-cavalry general, with an office opening matching the three excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted to chariot-and-cavalry general with the full ceremonial establishment of the three dukes.

sentences.zh: 祜上表固讓曰：

translations.literal: Hu submitted a memorial firmly declining, saying,
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized in firm refusal, writing:

sentences.zh: 臣伏聞恩詔，拔臣使同台司。

translations.literal: Your subject has bowed head and heard the gracious edict promoting your subject to stand beside the Three Offices.
translations.idiomatic: “I have received the edict elevating me to rank with the three great offices.”

sentences.zh: 臣自出身以來，適十數年，受任外內，每極顯重之任。

translations.literal: Since your subject first took office, there have been only ten-odd years; receiving appointments inside and without, each time it was at the utmost of prominent weight.
translations.idiomatic: “In the dozen years since I first served I have been given post after post of the highest responsibility, at court and in the field.”

sentences.zh: 常以智力不可頓進，恩寵不可久謬，夙夜戰悚，以榮為憂。

translations.literal: Constantly your subject thought that intelligence and strength cannot be advanced all at once, that favor and grace cannot long be wrongly held; night and day he trembled and took honor as a worry.
translations.idiomatic: “I have always known that talent cannot be rushed nor imperial favor indefinitely presumed; I have lain awake fearing that very distinction.”

sentences.zh: 臣聞古人之言，德未為人所服而受高爵，則使才臣不進；

translations.literal: Your subject has heard the words of the ancients: if virtue has not been submitted to by others yet one receives high noble rank, then it makes able ministers not advance;
translations.idiomatic: “The ancients said: reward high rank before the realm acknowledges your virtue, and true talent stops coming forward.”

sentences.zh: 功未為人所歸而荷厚祿，則使勞臣不勸。

translations.literal: if merit has not been turned to by others yet one bears thick emolument, then it makes laboring ministers not strive.
translations.idiomatic: “Pay rich emoluments before the realm credits your deeds, and diligent officers lose heart.”

sentences.zh: 今臣身托外戚，事連運會，誡在過寵，不患見遺。

translations.literal: Now your subject’s person relies on affines by marriage, affairs join the turning of the mandate—truly he is in excessive favor and does not fear being left out.
translations.idiomatic: “I am an imperial in-law riding a lucky moment; I am already overfavored and hardly risk being forgotten.”

sentences.zh: 而猥降發中之詔，加非次之榮。

translations.literal: Yet vulgarly there descends a deliberation-from-within edict and is added glory beyond the proper sequence.
translations.idiomatic: “Yet now an inner-court edict heaps on me honors out of turn.”

sentences.zh: 臣有何功可以堪之，何心可以安之。

translations.literal: With what merit can your subject bear it, with what heart can he accept it?
translations.idiomatic: “What deed of mine could justify this, what conscience could quietly accept it?”

sentences.zh: 身辱高位，傾覆尋至，願守先人弊廬，豈可得哉！

translations.literal: Body disgraced with high position, overturning follows soon—he wishes to keep his ancestors’ poor hut—how could he obtain that!
translations.idiomatic: “High place without desert brings ruin; I would rather live in my forebears’ mean cottage—yet even that modest wish is denied me!”

sentences.zh: 違命誠忤天威，曲從即復若此。

translations.literal: To disobey the command would truly affront Heaven’s might; to yield to persuasion would still be like this again.
translations.idiomatic: “Refusal offends the throne; compliance still leaves me in this impossible bind.”

sentences.zh: 蓋聞古人申于見知，大臣之節，不可則止。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that the ancients extended themselves before those who knew them; the integrity of great ministers lies in stopping when it is not possible.
translations.idiomatic: “The old model is to give one’s utmost to a ruler who understands you, and to withdraw when the way is blocked.”

sentences.zh: 臣雖小人，敢緣所蒙，念存斯義。

translations.literal: Though your subject is a petty man, he dares, relying on what he has received, to keep this principle in mind.
translations.idiomatic: “Small man though I am, I dare cling to that principle because of what I owe the state.”

sentences.zh: 今天下自服化以來，方漸八年，雖側席求賢，不遺幽賤，然臣不爾推有德，達有功，使聖聽知勝臣者多，未達者不少。

translations.literal: Now since the realm submitted to transformation, it has been barely eight years; though the ruler leaves his mat to seek worth and neglects no one in the darkest and humblest places—yet your subject has been unable to raise the virtuous and advance the meritorious, so that the sagely hearing would know many surpass your subject and no few have not yet risen.
translations.idiomatic: “Eight years have passed since the new order began; though Your Majesty seeks talent in every corner, I have still not lifted up the worthy or brought forward men of proven merit, so that many who excel me remain unknown to your ears.”

sentences.zh: 假令有遺德於版築之下，有隱才于屠釣之間，而朝議用臣不以為非，臣處之不以為愧，所失豈不大哉！

translations.literal: Suppose someone with virtue abandoned below the builder’s scaffolding, or talent hidden between butcher and fisher—yet court discussion would employ your subject without judging it wrong and your subject would stand in the post without shame—how great the loss would be!
translations.idiomatic: “Were there a sage laboring among masons or a genius selling meat by the river, and the court still thought me the right choice while I felt no shame—think what the realm would lose!”

sentences.zh: 臣忝竊雖久，未若今日兼文武之極寵，等宰輔之高位也。

translations.literal: Your subject’s unworthy tenure has been long, but never like today when he combines extreme favor of both civil and martial standing equal to the highest of ministers.
translations.idiomatic: “I have long held unworthy office, but never have I combined such civil and military honors with rank beside the chief ministers.”

sentences.zh: 且臣雖所見者狹，據今光祿大夫李憙執節高亮，在公正色；

translations.literal: Moreover, though what your subject has seen is narrow, according to what is before him now, Grandee of the Golden Seal Li Xi wields integrity high and bright, holds firm countenance in the public hall;
translations.idiomatic: “Moreover, limited though my view is, Grandee Li Xi stands for stern integrity in open court;

sentences.zh: 光祿大夫魯芝潔身寡欲，和而不同；

translations.literal: Grandee of the Golden Seal Lu Zhi cleanses his person with few desires, harmonizes yet does not conform blindly;
translations.idiomatic: Grandee Lu Zhi lives sparingly, agrees without flattering;

sentences.zh: 光祿大夫李胤清亮簡素，立身在朝，皆服事華髮，以禮終始。

translations.literal: Grandee of the Golden Seal Li Yin is clear bright plain simple, establishes his person at court; all have served until florid hair in age and from beginning to end observed ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Grandee Li Yin is lucid, frugal, and upright; all three have grown gray in service and kept ritual to the end.

sentences.zh: 雖歷位外內之寵，不異寒賤之家，而猶未蒙此選，臣更越之，何以塞天下之望，少益日月！

translations.literal: Though they have enjoyed favor inside and out without differing from poor mean families, still they have not received this selection—how much more does your subject exceed them: how would he block the expectations of the realm or slightly benefit the sun and moon!
translations.idiomatic: “Though honored at court and in camp they live no better than poor households, none has been singled out like this—how much less should I, who surpass none of them, answer the world’s hopes or add luster to your reign!”

sentences.zh: 是以誓心守節，無苟進之志。

translations.literal: On this account he has sworn his heart to guard integrity and has no mind to advance through improper means.
translations.idiomatic: “Therefore I have resolved to keep my integrity and refuse rank gained by improper paths.”

sentences.zh: 今道路行通，方隅多事，乞留前恩，使臣得速還屯。

translations.literal: Now the roads run clear and borders see many affairs; he begs to retain the earlier grace and let your subject speedily return to his garrison.
translations.idiomatic: “The roads are open again and the frontiers are restless; I beg you to honor your earlier favor and let me hurry back to my command.”

sentences.zh: 不爾留連，必于外虞有闕。

translations.literal: If not, lingering on will surely leave a gap in outer defense.
translations.idiomatic: “Otherwise my delay here will surely weaken the outer defenses.”

sentences.zh: 匹夫之志，有不可奪。

translations.literal: The resolve of a common man may be something that cannot be taken from him.
translations.idiomatic: “Even a commoner’s settled purpose cannot be wrested away.”

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: They did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The throne refused his plea.

sentences.zh: 及還鎮，吳西陵督步闡舉城來降。

translations.literal: When he returned to his command, Wu’s Stone Citadel superintendent Bu Chan raised the city to defect.
translations.idiomatic: Back at his post, he saw Bu Chan, Wu’s commander at Xiling, surrender the city to Jin.

sentences.zh: 吳將陸抗攻之甚急，詔祜迎闡。

translations.literal: Wu general Lu Kang attacked it urgently; an edict ordered Hu to go meet Chan.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Kang pressed the siege hard; an edict told Yang Hu to march to relieve Bu Chan.

sentences.zh: 祜率兵五萬出江陵，遣荊州刺史楊肇攻抗，不克，闡竟為抗所擒。

translations.literal: Hu led fifty thousand troops out of Jiangling and sent Jingzhou Inspector Yang Zhao to attack Kang; he could not prevail; Chan was finally captured by Kang.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hu took fifty thousand men from Jiangling and sent Inspector Yang Zhao against Lu Kang; Zhao failed, and Bu Chan fell to Lu Kang in the end.

sentences.zh: 有司奏：「祜所統八萬餘人，賊眾不過三萬。

translations.literal: The relevant offices memorialized: “The troops Hu commanded were over eighty thousand; the bandits numbered no more than thirty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Censors wrote: “Yang Hu had more than eighty thousand men; the enemy fewer than thirty thousand.”

sentences.zh: 祜頓兵江陵，使賊備得設。

translations.literal: Hu halted troops at Jiangling and let the bandits complete their preparations.
translations.idiomatic: “He sat at Jiangling and let the foe finish their dispositions.”

sentences.zh: 乃遣楊肇偏軍入險，兵少糧懸，軍人挫衄。

translations.literal: He then sent Yang Zhao’s detached force into perilous terrain—few soldiers, supplies hanging in balance, the army suffered setback and defeat.
translations.idiomatic: “He then pushed Yang Zhao’s column into difficult ground with too few men and precarious supplies, and the army was beaten.”

sentences.zh: 背違詔命，無大臣節。

translations.literal: He turned against the edict’s orders and lacked the integrity of a great minister.
translations.idiomatic: “He disobeyed imperial strategy and failed the standard of a chief minister.”

sentences.zh: 可免官，以侯就第。

translations.literal: He may be dismissed from office and demoted to commoner status at his marquis residence.”
translations.idiomatic: “Strip him of office and send him home as a commoner marquis.”

sentences.zh: 」竟坐貶為平南將軍，而免楊肇為庶人。

translations.literal: In the end he was for that demoted to General Who Pacifies the South, and Yang Zhao was dismissed to commoner.
translations.idiomatic: In the end Yang Hu was demoted to general who pacifies the south and Yang Zhao reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 祜以孟獻營武牢而鄭人懼，晏弱城東陽而萊子服，乃進據險耍，開建五城，收膏腴之地，奪吳人之資，石城以西，盡為晉有。

translations.literal: Hu took it that when Meng Xian camped at Wulao the people of Zheng were fearful, and when Yan Ruo walled Dongyang the lord of Lai submitted; then he advanced to occupy critical choke points, opened and built five fortresses, seized fertile land, wrested the Wu people’s resources, and west of Stone City all came under Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Reasoning from Meng Xian’s camp at Wulao, which terrified Zheng, and Yan Ruo’s fort at Dongyang, which broke Lai, he seized key terrain, raised five strongpoints, took rich farmland, and deprived Wu of resources until everything west of Stone City belonged to Jin.

sentences.zh: 自是前後降者不絕，乃增修德信，以懷柔初附，慨然有吞併之心。

translations.literal: From this time defectors before and after were unending; then he increased cultivation of virtue and good faith to soothe those newly attached, and was moved with a mind to swallow and annex.
translations.idiomatic: Defections then flowed without cease; he doubled down on good faith toward new subjects and began to contemplate full conquest.

sentences.zh: 每與吳人交兵，克日方戰，不為掩襲之計。

translations.literal: Whenever he crossed arms with Wu men, he chose the day to fight and did not use masking ambush plans.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he fought Wu troops he fixed a battle day in advance and refused sneak attacks.

sentences.zh: 將帥有欲進譎詐之策者，輒飲以醇酒，使不得言。

translations.literal: When generals wished to advance devious stratagems, he would give them strong wine to drink so they could not speak.
translations.idiomatic: If a subordinate proposed a ruse, Yang Hu plied him with strong wine until the idea went unspoken.

sentences.zh: 人有略吳二兒為俘者，祜遣送還其家。

translations.literal: When someone seized two Wu children as captives, Hu sent them back to their families.
translations.idiomatic: When two Wu boys were taken prisoner, he sent them home.

sentences.zh: 後吳將夏詳、邵顗等來降，二兒之父亦率其屬與俱。

translations.literal: Later when Wu generals Xia Xiang and Shao Yi came to surrender, the two boys’ fathers also led their followers with them.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Wu generals Xia Xiang and Shao Yi defected, those boys’ fathers came over with their men as well.

sentences.zh: 吳將陳尚、潘景來寇，祜追斬之，美其死節而厚加殯斂。

translations.literal: When Wu generals Chen Shang and Pan Jing came raiding, Hu pursued and executed them, admired their dying with integrity, and gave them generous burial.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shang and Pan Jing raided his lines; he hunted them down and killed them, then honored their loyalty with a full burial.

sentences.zh: 景、尚子弟迎喪，祜以禮遣還。

translations.literal: Jing’s and Shang’s sons and younger brothers came to greet the coffins; Hu sent them back with courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Their sons came for the bodies; he saw them off with ritual courtesy.

sentences.zh: 吳將鄧香掠夏口，祜募生縛香，既至，宥之。

translations.literal: When Wu general Deng Xiang plundered Xiakou, Hu hired men to capture him alive; when he arrived, Hu pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Wu’s Deng Xiang raided Xiakou; Yang Hu offered a reward for his capture alive, then released him when he was brought in.

sentences.zh: 香感其恩甚，率部曲而降。

translations.literal: Xiang was deeply moved by this grace and led his personal following to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Grateful for the mercy, Deng Xiang brought his entire command over to Jin.

sentences.zh: 祜出軍行吳境，刈穀為糧，皆計所侵，送絹償之。

translations.literal: When Hu led troops through Wu territory and cut grain for provisions, he calculated what was taken and sent silk to compensate.
translations.idiomatic: When his army requisitioned grain in Wu lands, he reckoned the amount and paid silk in compensation.

sentences.zh: 每會眾江沔游獵，常止晉地。

translations.literal: Whenever he gathered multitudes to hunt along the Jiang and Han, he always stopped on Jin ground.
translations.idiomatic: Mass hunts along the Han always stayed on Jin soil.

sentences.zh: 若禽獸先為吳人所傷而為晉兵所得者，皆封還之。

translations.literal: If game had first been wounded by Wu people but was obtained by Jin troops, he had it all sealed and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Game first hit by Wu hunters but picked up by his men was wrapped and sent back across the line.

sentences.zh: 於是吳人翕然悅服，稱為羊公，不之名也。

translations.literal: Thereupon Wu people were uniformly pleased and submitted, calling him Duke Yang without speaking his personal name.
translations.idiomatic: Wu’s soldiers and farmers came to admire him as “Lord Yang,” using a title instead of his given name.

sentences.zh: 祜與陸抗相對，使命交通，抗稱祜之德量，雖樂毅、諸葛孔明不能過也。

translations.literal: Hu faced Lu Kang; envoys passed between them; Kang praised Hu’s virtue and capacity, saying that even Yue Yi and Zhuge Liang could not surpass him.
translations.idiomatic: Facing Lu Kang across the border, he exchanged envoys; Lu Kang said his moral stature outshone even Yue Yi or Zhuge Liang.

sentences.zh: 抗嘗病，祜饋之藥，抗服之無疑心。

translations.literal: Kang once fell ill; Hu sent him medicine; Kang took it without suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Kang fell ill, Yang Hu sent him medicine; Lu Kang drank it without doubting treachery.

sentences.zh: 人多諫抗，抗曰：「羊祜豈鴆人者！

translations.literal: Many people remonstrated with Kang; Kang said, "Could Yang Hu be a man who poisons others!"
translations.idiomatic: His officers warned Lu Kang, who replied, "Yang Hu is no poisoner."

sentences.zh: 」時談以為華元、子反復見於今日。

translations.literal: " At the time discussion held that Hua Yuan and Zifan had appeared again in the present day.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries said their courtesy recalled Hua Yuan and the Chu commander Zifan.

sentences.zh: 抗每告其戍曰：「彼專為德，我專為暴，是不戰而自服也。

translations.literal: Kang repeatedly told his garrison commanders, "They devote themselves to kindness; we devote ourselves to harshness—then they yield without a battle."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Kang told his men, "The Jin side cultivates virtue while we rely on force, so they can win hearts without fighting."

sentences.zh: 各保分界而已，無求細利。

translations.literal: "Each side should merely hold its own frontier and not chase petty advantage."
translations.idiomatic: He ordered each command to guard its own line and avoid risky skirmishes for small gain.

sentences.zh: 」孫皓聞二境交和，以詰抗。

translations.literal: " When Sun Hao heard that the two borders were treating each other with courtesy, he rebuked Lu Kang.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Hao learned the frontiers had grown almost cordial, he called Lu Kang to account.

sentences.zh: 抗曰：「一邑一鄉，不可以無信義，況大國乎！

translations.literal: Kang said, "Even a single town or village cannot do without good faith—how much less a great state!"
translations.idiomatic: Lu Kang answered, "A village cannot live without trust, let alone a kingdom."

sentences.zh: 臣不如此，正是彰其德，於祜無傷也。」

translations.literal: "Your subject acts in this way precisely to display his virtue; it does no harm to Yang Hu."
translations.idiomatic: "By behaving generously I only highlight his integrity; I do not injure Yang Hu."

sentences.zh: 祜貞愨無私，疾惡邪佞，旬勖、馮紞之徒甚忌之。

translations.literal: Hu was chaste and sincere without selfishness, hated evil and sycophancy; Xun Xu, Feng Yi, and their sort greatly resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hu was upright and disdained flatterers; Xun Xu and Feng Yi therefore bore him a grudge.

sentences.zh: 從甥王衍嘗詣祜陳事，辭甚俊辨，祜不然之，衍拂衣而起。

translations.literal: His sister's son Wang Yan once visited Hu to state affairs; his words were very sharp in debate; Hu did not approve; Yan flung his sleeves and rose.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Wang Yan once came to argue a point with brilliant rhetoric; Yang Hu disagreed, and Wang Yan stormed off.

sentences.zh: 祜顧謂賓客曰：「王夷甫方以盛名處大位，然敗俗傷化，必此人也。

translations.literal: Hu looked back and said to the guests, "Wang Yanfu will soon by great reputation occupy high position, yet to ruin custom and injure transformation—surely it will be this man."
translations.idiomatic: Turning to his guests Yang Hu said, "Wang Yan will ride fame to high office—and he will be the man who corrupts public morals."

sentences.zh: 」步闡之役，祜以軍法將斬王戎，故戎、衍並憾之，每言論多毀祜。

translations.literal: " In the Bu Chan affair, Hu by military law was about to execute Wang Rong; therefore Rong and Yan both resented him and often in discourse largely slandered Hu.
translations.idiomatic: During the Bu Chan campaign Yang Hu had nearly executed Wang Rong by martial law, so Wang Rong and Wang Yan slandered him at every turn.

sentences.zh: 時人為之語曰：「二王當國，羊公無德。」

translations.literal: At the time people made a rhyme of it: "When the two Wangs run the state, Duke Yang has no virtue."
translations.idiomatic: A popular jingle ran, "With the Wangs in power, good Duke Yang has no virtue left."

sentences.zh: 咸甯初，除征南大將軍、開府儀同三司，得專辟召。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianning he was appointed General Who Conquers the South and Grand Marshal with an establishment equaling the three excellencies, obtaining sole authority to summon and appoint staff.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xianning era he became general who conquers the south with a grand marshal's establishment matching the three dukes, and sole power to recruit officers.

sentences.zh: 初，祐以伐吳必藉上流之勢。

translations.literal: Earlier, Hu had held that to conquer Wu one must rely on the advantage of the upper Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hu had long believed a conquest of Wu required pressure from upstream.

sentences.zh: 又時吳有童謠曰：「阿童復阿童，銜刀浮渡江。

translations.literal: Also at that time Wu had a children's rhyme saying, "A-tong, again A-tong, biting a knife floats across the river."
translations.idiomatic: A Wu children's song ran, "A-tong, again A-tong, knife in teeth, floats across the river."

sentences.zh: 不畏岸上獸，但畏水中龍。

translations.literal: "Do not fear the beasts on the bank; only fear the dragon in the water."
translations.idiomatic: "Fear not the beasts on shore—fear the dragon in the water."

sentences.zh: 」祜聞之曰：「此必水軍有功，但當思應其名者耳。

translations.literal: " When Hu heard it he said, "This surely means the navy will win the glory; one has only to think who fits that name."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hu said, "That points to a naval hero; we need only find the man the nickname fits."

sentences.zh: 」會益州刺史王濬徵為大司農，祜知其可任，濬又小字阿童，因表留浚監益州諸軍事，加龍驤將軍，密令修舟楫，為順流之計。

translations.literal: " It happened that the Inspector of Yizhou Wang Jun was summoned to be Minister of Agriculture; Hu knew he could be entrusted; Jun's childhood name was also A-tong; therefore he memorialized to retain Jun as supervisor of all military affairs in Yizhou, added General Who Soars like a Dragon, and secretly ordered him to build boats for a downstream campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun of Yizhou was recalled to the capital as minister of agriculture; Yang Hu knew his talent and that his pet name was A-tong, so he kept Wang Jun in the west as area commander with the title general who soars like a dragon and secretly had him build a river fleet.

sentences.zh: 祜繕甲訓卒，廣為戎備。

translations.literal: Hu repaired armor and trained soldiers and broadly prepared for war.
translations.idiomatic: He repaired arms, drilled troops, and expanded frontier preparations.

sentences.zh: 至是上疏曰：

translations.literal: Thereupon he submitted a memorial saying,
translations.idiomatic: He then memorialized the throne as follows.

sentences.zh: 先帝順天應時，西平巴蜀，南和吳會，海內得以休息，兆庶有樂安之心。

translations.literal: The former emperor complied with Heaven and answered the times, pacified Ba and Shu in the west, reconciled Wu and Yue in the south, so that within the seas could rest and the myriad commoners had a mind of peace and joy.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor moved with the times: he subdued Ba–Shu in the west, made peace with Wu and Yue in the south, and gave the realm a respite so the people could breathe.

sentences.zh: 而吳復背信，使邊事更興。

translations.literal: Yet Wu again betrayed trust, causing border affairs to arise anew.
translations.idiomatic: Wu broke faith again, and the frontier flared up once more.

sentences.zh: 夫期運雖天所授，而功業必由人而成，不一大舉掃滅，則眾役無時得安。

translations.literal: Now though allotted fortune is what Heaven confers, merit and enterprise must be completed by men; unless we mount one great expedition to sweep them away, corvée and garrison duty will never know peace.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven sets the timing, but men must finish the work; without one decisive campaign to destroy Wu, endless mobilizations will never end.

sentences.zh: 亦所以隆先帝之勳，成無為之化也。

translations.literal: This is also thereby to magnify the former emperor's merit and complete the transformation of non-action.
translations.idiomatic: Victory would crown your father's enterprise and bring the realm the quiet of true non-interference.

sentences.zh: 故堯有丹水之伐，舜有三苗之征，咸以寧靜宇宙，戢兵和眾者也。

translations.literal: Therefore Yao campaigned at the Dan River, Shun chastised the Three Miao—all to still the universe, sheath the weapons, and harmonize the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: Yao fought at Dan, Shun punished the Three Miao: both used force once to still the world and put arms away for good.

sentences.zh: 蜀平之時，天下皆謂吳當並亡，自此來十三年，是謂一周，平定之期復在今日矣。

translations.literal: At the time Shu fell, everyone under Heaven said Wu would perish with it; from that time thirteen years have passed—this completes one cycle; the moment to pacify them is again today.
translations.idiomatic: When Shu fell, all expected Wu to follow; thirteen years have passed—a full cycle—and the hour to finish Wu is again at hand.

sentences.zh: 議者常言吳楚有道後服，無禮先強，此乃謂侯之時耳。

translations.literal: Discussers often say that Wu and Chu submit late when the ruler possesses the Way and grow arrogant when ritual fails—this language applies only to the age of the feudal lords.
translations.idiomatic: The old saying that Wu and Chu yield last when virtue rules and turn fierce when it does not described the age of rival feudatories, not a unified empire.

sentences.zh: 當今一統，不得與古同諭。

translations.literal: Now under single unification, one cannot argue by the same measure as antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Under a single throne the old parallel no longer holds.

sentences.zh: 夫適道之論，皆未應權，是故謀之雖多，而決之欲獨。

translations.literal: As for doctrines that fit abstract principle, none meets present exigency; therefore though counsel is plentiful, the decision must rest with one man.
translations.idiomatic: High-minded theories miss practical needs; many voices argue, yet one ruler must decide.

sentences.zh: 凡以險阻得存者，謂所敵者同，力足自固。

translations.literal: Those who survive behind natural barriers assume their foe is evenly matched and their own strength enough to hold fast.
translations.idiomatic: Mountain defenses help only when the enemy is comparable and your own force can hold.

sentences.zh: 苟其輕重不齊，強弱異勢，則智士不能謀，而險阻不可保也。

translations.literal: If weight of numbers and balance of power do not match, the cleverest planner cannot save the situation and barriers cannot be relied on.
translations.idiomatic: When strength is uneven, no genius of strategy and no cliff will save a state.

sentences.zh: 蜀之為國，非不險也，高山尋雲霓，深谷肆無景，束馬懸車，然後得濟，皆言一夫荷戟，千人莫當。

translations.literal: The state of Shu was not without peril: peaks pierced the clouds, gorges were sunless; horses were hobbled and carts winched—only then could one cross; men said one soldier at a pass could block a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Shu was famously impassable—cloud-capped peaks, lightless ravines, roads that needed roped carts—yet legend said one halberdier could hold a thousand.

sentences.zh: 及進兵之日，曾無籓籬之限，斬將搴旗，伏屍數萬，乘勝席捲，徑至成都，漢中諸城，皆鳥棲而不敢出。

translations.literal: When our army advanced, there was not even a palisade to stop them: generals fell, banners were taken, tens of thousands died; victory rolled on to Chengdu while Hanzhong's garrisons cowered in their forts like roosting birds.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when we marched, no fence held us back: we cut down commanders, seized flags, left tens of thousands dead, swept straight to Chengdu, and every Hanzhong fort hid like a bird in a roost.

sentences.zh: 非皆無戰心，誠力不足相抗。

translations.literal: It was not that they lacked the will to fight—they simply lacked strength to resist.
translations.idiomatic: It was not cowardice; they were overmatched.

sentences.zh: 至劉禪降服，諸營堡者索然俱散。

translations.literal: When Liu Shan surrendered, every camp and stockade melted away.
translations.idiomatic: The moment Liu Shan yielded, Shu’s strongpoints collapsed.

sentences.zh: 今江淮之難，不過劍閣；

translations.literal: Now the Yangzi–Huai obstacle is no worse than Sword Gate;
translations.idiomatic: The Yangzi–Huai line is no tougher than Jianmen Pass.

sentences.zh: 山川之險，不過岷漢；

translations.literal: The mountain and river terrain is no worse than the Min and Han gorges;
translations.idiomatic: Its mountains and rivers are no worse than the Min and Han gorges.

sentences.zh: 孫皓之暴，侈于劉禪；

translations.literal: Sun Hao's cruelty exceeds Liu Shan's;
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao is more vicious than Liu Shan was.

sentences.zh: 吳人之困，甚于巴蜀。

translations.literal: The distress of the Wu people is greater than that of Ba and Shu.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu populace is more exhausted than Ba–Shu ever was.

sentences.zh: 而大晉兵眾，多於前世；

translations.literal: Yet the armies of great Jin are more numerous than in former ages;
translations.idiomatic: Jin fields larger armies than the Wei ever did.

sentences.zh: 資儲器械，盛於往時；

translations.literal: Supplies and weapons are richer than in times past.
translations.idiomatic: Our stores and matériel surpass earlier campaigns.

sentences.zh: 今不于此平吳，而更阻兵相守，征夫苦役，日尋干戈，經歷盛衰，不可長久，宜當時定，以一四海。

translations.literal: If we do not crush Wu now but keep armies locked in stalemate, conscripts will wear out under endless alarms; states cannot swing forever between boom and ruin—this must be settled now to unify the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Delay means endless mobilizations and skittish garrisons; prosperity and decay cannot alternate forever—we should settle Wu now and bind the four seas under one rule.

sentences.zh: 今若引梁益之兵水陸俱下，荊楚之眾進臨江陵，平南、豫州，直指夏口，徐、揚、青、兗並向秣陵，鼓旆以疑之，多方以誤之，以一隅之吳，當天下之眾，勢分形散，所備皆急，巴漢奇兵出其空虛，一處傾壞，則上下震盪。

translations.literal: Now if Liang and Yi strike by land and water together, Jing and Chu press on Jiangling, Pacifies-the-South and Yu province drive on Xiakou, Xu, Yang, Qing, and Yan converge on Moling, drums and banners feint everywhere to confuse them, and Ba–Han shock columns strike their weak points—Wu, a single corner against the world, will be stretched thin; one breach will shake them from top to bottom.
translations.idiomatic: Send Liang and Yi downriver by land and sea, push Jing and Chu against Jiangling, aim Pacifies-the-South and Yu at Xiakou, march Xu, Yang, Qing, and Yan on Moling, feint on every front, then thrust from Ba and Han into the gaps—Wu cannot cover a thousand leagues of river; one rupture will shatter the whole.

sentences.zh: 吳緣江為國，無有內外，東西數千里，以籓籬自持，所敵者大，無有寧息。

translations.literal: Wu hugs the Yangzi for a thousand li without inner depth, trusting its bank like a fence while the enemy it faces is the entire realm—it never rests.
translations.idiomatic: Wu is a ribbon along the river, east to west for thousands of li, with no strategic depth; it braces like a palisade against a continent-wide foe and never rests.

sentences.zh: 孫皓孫恣情任意，與下多忌，名臣重將不復自信，是以孫秀之徒皆畏逼而至。

translations.literal: Sun Hao indulges every whim, suspects his ministers, so that famed generals no longer trust their own judgment—hence men like Sun Xiu fled here in fear.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao indulges himself, doubts his best men, and has driven officers such as Sun Xiu to defect in terror.

sentences.zh: 將疑於朝，士困於野，無有保世之計，一定之心。

translations.literal: Generals doubt the court; soldiers languish in the field; they have no plan to save their houses and no fixed loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Commanders second-guess the throne while troops waste in the mud; no one has a long-term plan or settled allegiance.

sentences.zh: 平常之日，猶懷去就，兵臨之際，必有應者，終不能齊力致死，已可知也。

translations.literal: In peacetime they already think of changing sides; when our hosts appear, many will answer the call—they will never unite their strength to fight to the death, as is already plain.
translations.idiomatic: Even in quiet times they weigh defection; under invasion they will break ranks—they cannot mount a unanimous fight to the death.

sentences.zh: 其俗急速，不能持久，弓弩戟盾不如中國，唯有水戰是其所便。

translations.literal: Their temper is hasty; they cannot endure long campaigns; crossbows, halberds, and shields are inferior to ours—only on water do they feel at home.
translations.idiomatic: They are impetuous, ill suited to long wars, and weaker than our infantry arms—river fighting is their sole advantage.

sentences.zh: 一入其境，則長江非復所固，還保城池，則去長入短。

translations.literal: Once we enter their land, the Long River ceases to be a sure shield; if they fall back to cities, they trade length for shortness and lose mobility.
translations.idiomatic: Once we are ashore, the great river stops protecting them; if they hide in towns, they trade mobility for siege.

sentences.zh: 而官軍懸進，人有致節之志，吳人戰於其內，有憑城之心。

translations.literal: Yet our troops advance with zeal while Wu fights at home behind walls—each side has its own edge.
translations.idiomatic: Our men march with elated purpose; Wu's soldiers fight at home behind ramparts—each side plays to a different strength.

sentences.zh: 如此，軍不逾時，克可必矣。

translations.literal: In such conditions the campaign need not drag on; victory can be assured.
translations.idiomatic: Under these conditions the war need not linger; success is certain.

sentences.zh: 帝深納之。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted the plan in full.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor embraced his analysis.

sentences.zh: 會秦涼屢敗，祜復表曰：「吳平則胡自定，但當速濟大功耳。

translations.literal: It happened that Qin and Liang suffered repeated defeats; Hu again memorialized, saying, "When Wu falls, the northern tribes will settle of themselves—only finish the great task quickly."
translations.idiomatic: While Qin and Liang kept losing, Yang Hu wrote again: "Crush Wu and the steppe troubles cure themselves—only strike the decisive blow at once."

sentences.zh: 」而議者多不同，祜歎曰：「天下不如意，恆十居七八，故有當斷不斷。

translations.literal: " Yet most advisers disagreed; Hu sighed, "Under Heaven, seven or eight times in ten things go awry; hence there is the fault of failing to decide when one should."
translations.idiomatic: The court still hesitated; Yang Hu sighed that most plans miscarry because rulers shrink from the moment to act.

sentences.zh: 天與不取，豈非更事者恨于後時哉！」

translations.literal: "When Heaven offers a prize and you refuse it, will not later statesmen regret the delay!"
translations.idiomatic: "Heaven hands you victory; to refuse it is to invite the regret of every statesman who came too late."

sentences.zh: 其後，詔以泰山之南武陽、牟、南城、梁父、平陽五縣為南城郡，封祜為南城侯，置相，與郡公同。

translations.literal: Later an edict took five counties south of Mount Tai—Wuyang, Mou, Nancheng, Liangfu, and Pingyang—and formed Nancheng commandery, enfeoffing Hu as marquis of Nancheng with a chancellor, equal to a commandery duke.
translations.idiomatic: The court later carved five Taishan counties into Nancheng commandery and made Yang Hu marquis of Nancheng with ducal privileges.

sentences.zh: 祜讓曰：「昔張良請受留萬戶，漢祖不奪其志。

translations.literal: Hu declined, saying, "Long ago Zhang Liang asked only for ten thousand households at Liu, and the Han founder did not force his wish."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hu refused: "Zhang Liang asked only for ten thousand households at Liu, and Gaozu respected his modesty."

sentences.zh: 臣受钜平於先帝，敢辱重爵，以速官謗！

translations.literal: "Your subject received Juping from the former emperor; how dare he insult a lofty title and hasten censorious talk!"
translations.idiomatic: "I received Juping from the late emperor; I cannot accept a grander patent and invite scandal."

sentences.zh: 」固執不拜，帝許之。

translations.literal: " He held firm and would not bow acceptance; the emperor permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: He stood his ground until the emperor let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 祜每被登進，常守沖退，至心素著，故特見申於分列之外。

translations.literal: Whenever Hu was promoted, he kept to modest withdrawal; his sincere simplicity was well known, so he received extraordinary favor outside the usual allotments.
translations.idiomatic: Each promotion found him pleading modesty; his transparent sincerity won him unusual indulgence.

sentences.zh: 是以名德遠播，朝野具瞻，搢紳僉議，當居台輔。

translations.literal: Therefore his fame spread through court and countryside; gentry agreed he ought to stand among the highest ministers.
translations.idiomatic: His reputation filled court and capital; the elite expected him to join the chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 帝方有兼併之志，仗祜以東南之任，故寢之。

translations.literal: The emperor was bent on annexation and relied on Hu for the southeast, so he set the matter aside.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor still needed him on the southeastern front, so he shelved the promotion.

sentences.zh: 祜曆職二朝，任典樞要，政事損益，皆諮訪焉，勢利之求，無所關與。

translations.literal: Hu served two reigns, held the pivot of policy—gains and losses in government were referred to him—and he never mixed in quests for power or profit.
translations.idiomatic: He steered two reigns at the center of power, shaped every major decision, and never traded policy for private gain.

sentences.zh: 其嘉謀讜議，皆焚其草，故世莫聞。

translations.literal: His fine plans and blunt advice he burned in draft, so the world never heard them.
translations.idiomatic: He burned drafts of his best counsel, leaving no paper trail.

sentences.zh: 凡所進達，人皆不知所由。

translations.literal: Those he recommended never knew through whom they had risen.
translations.idiomatic: Men he advanced seldom learned they owed their posts to him.

sentences.zh: 或謂祜慎密太過者，祜曰：「是何言歟！

translations.literal: Someone said Hu was over-careful; Hu said, "What talk is this!"
translations.idiomatic: When told he was too secretive, he exclaimed, "What nonsense!"

sentences.zh: 夫入則造膝，出則詭辭，君臣不密之誡，吾惟懼其不及。

translations.literal: "To speak intimately indoors yet speak evasively outdoors—that is the warning against lack of secrecy between ruler and subject; I only fear falling short of that standard."
translations.idiomatic: "Close counsel in private and guarded words in public are what loyal ministers owe; I worry only that I fall short."

sentences.zh: 不能舉賢取異，豈得不愧知人之難哉！

translations.literal: "If I cannot raise the worthy and gather the unusual, how can I not feel ashamed before the difficulty of knowing men!"
translations.idiomatic: "If I fail to lift able men, I shame the art of knowing others."

sentences.zh: 且拜爵公朝，謝恩私門，吾所不取。」

translations.literal: "Moreover to receive rank in the public court and give thanks in a private gate—that I will not do."
translations.idiomatic: "I will not take titles in the audience hall and pay my debts of favor in some minister's doorway."

sentences.zh: 祜女夫嘗勸祜「有所營置，令有歸戴者，可不美乎？

translations.literal: Hu's son-in-law once urged him, "Arrange some patronage so men have someone to look up to—would it not be fine?"
translations.idiomatic: His son-in-law urged him to build a faction so clients would owe him gratitude.

sentences.zh: 」祜默然不應，退告諸子曰：「此可謂知其一不知其二。

translations.literal: " Hu was silent and did not answer; retiring he told his sons, "This can be called knowing one side but not the other."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hu said nothing, then told his sons, "That man knows half the truth."

sentences.zh: 人臣樹私則背公，是大惑也。

translations.literal: "When ministers cultivate private factions, they betray the public—this is great delusion."
translations.idiomatic: "Ministers who chase private networks betray the state—that is folly."

sentences.zh: 汝宜識吾此意。

translations.literal: "You ought to understand my meaning in this."
translations.idiomatic: "Remember what I mean."

sentences.zh: 」嘗與從弟琇書曰：「既定邊事，當角巾東路，歸故里，為容棺之墟。

translations.literal: " He once wrote to cousin Xiu, saying, "Once the border is settled, I shall tie a hermit's kerchief, take the eastern road home, and find a hill to hold my coffin."
translations.idiomatic: He wrote his cousin Yang Xiu, "When the frontier is quiet I mean to retire eastward in scholar's scarf and choose a burial mound in my homeland."

sentences.zh: 以白士而居重位，何能不以盛滿受責乎！

translations.literal: "A plain commoner yet occupying a weighty post—how can one not earn blame when fullness overflows!"
translations.idiomatic: "A man of white cloth in a great office cannot escape blame when fortune crests."

sentences.zh: 疏廣是吾師也。」

translations.literal: Shu Guang is my teacher.
translations.idiomatic: Shu Guang is the man I take as my model.

sentences.zh: 祜樂山水，每風景，必造峴山，置酒言詠，終日不倦。

translations.literal: Hu loved mountains and rivers; whenever the scenery was fine, he would visit Xian Mountain, set out wine, speak and chant, all day without tiring.
translations.idiomatic: He loved landscape; on fine days he climbed Mount Xian, poured wine, and talked poetry until dusk.

sentences.zh: 嘗慨然歎息，顧謂從事中郎鄒湛等曰：「自有宇宙，便有此山。

translations.literal: Once he sighed, turned to his adjutant Zou Zhan and others, and said, "Since there has been a cosmos, there has been this mountain."
translations.idiomatic: Once he sighed to Zou Zhan and the rest, "This peak has stood since the world began."

sentences.zh: 由來賢達勝士，登此遠望，如我與卿者多矣！

translations.literal: "From antiquity worthies and superior men who climbed here to gaze afar—like you and I—how many have there been!"
translations.idiomatic: "How many sages climbed here, looked out like us, and vanished?"

sentences.zh: 皆湮滅無聞，使人悲傷。

translations.literal: All were extinguished without fame, which makes men grieve.
translations.idiomatic: They are forgotten, and that grieves me.

sentences.zh: 如百歲後有知，魂魄猶應登此也。

translations.literal: If after a hundred years there is awareness, soul and spirit ought still to climb here.
translations.idiomatic: If consciousness survives the grave, my ghost should climb here still.

sentences.zh: 」湛曰：「公德冠四海，道嗣前哲，令聞令望，必與此山俱傳。

translations.literal: " Zhan said, "Your lordship's virtue caps the four seas, his Way continues former sages; fair fame and fair hope will surely be transmitted together with this mountain."
translations.idiomatic: Zou Zhan replied, "Your virtue fills the realm, your teaching follows the ancients; your name will outlive this mountain."

sentences.zh: 至若湛輩，乃當如公言耳。」

translations.literal: "As for the likes of Zhan, it will be as your lordship said."
translations.idiomatic: "Men like me will be forgotten, just as you say."

sentences.zh: 祜當討吳賊功，將進爵土，乞以賜舅子蔡襲。

translations.literal: When Hu was about to be rewarded for the campaign against Wu's bandits and advanced in noble rank and fief, he begged to grant the honor to his maternal nephew's son Cai Xi.
translations.idiomatic: When honors for the Wu campaign were due, he asked that the patent go to his nephew Cai Xi.

sentences.zh: 詔封襲關內侯，邑三百戶。

translations.literal: An edict enfeoffed Xi as marquis within the passes, three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: The court made Cai Xi a marquis within the passes with three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 會吳人寇弋陽、江夏，略戶口，詔遣侍臣移書詰祐不追討之意，並欲移州復舊之宜。

translations.literal: It happened that Wu raided Yiyang and Jiangxia and carried off registered households; an edict sent a palace attendant with a letter demanding of Hu why he had not pursued, and asking about moving the provincial seat back to its former site.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu raided Yiyang and Jiangxia and abducted people, the court messenger pressed Yang Hu on his failure to pursue and on relocating the provincial headquarters.

sentences.zh: 祜曰：「江夏去襄陽八百里，比知賊問，賊去亦已經日矣。

translations.literal: Hu said, "Jiangxia is eight hundred li from Xiangyang; by the time we learn of the raid, the raiders have already been gone more than a day."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hu answered, "Jiangxia lies eight hundred li from Xiangyang; news arrives a day after the enemy has left."

sentences.zh: 步軍方往，安能救之哉！

translations.literal: Infantry is only then marching—how can it save them!
translations.idiomatic: Foot columns cannot arrive in time to help.

sentences.zh: 勞師以免責，恐非事宜也。

translations.literal: To weary the army in order to escape blame is probably not the suitable course.
translations.idiomatic: To march troops to exhaustion merely to satisfy critics would be worse policy.

sentences.zh: 昔魏武帝置都督，類皆與州相近，以兵勢好合惡離。

translations.literal: Formerly Wei Martial Emperor set area commanders generally close to their provinces, because military momentum likes union and dislikes separation.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao placed area commanders beside their provinces because armies fight best when concentrated.

sentences.zh: 疆埸之間，一彼一此，慎守而已，古之善教也。

translations.literal: Between border marches, now this side now that—careful guarding suffices; this is the good teaching of antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Frontiers shift; steady garrisoning is the ancient lesson.

sentences.zh: 若輒徙州，賊出無常，亦未知州之所宜據也。

translations.literal: If we rashly move the province, when bandits strike unpredictably we will not even know where the seat ought to stand.
translations.idiomatic: Hasty relocation would leave us guessing where to anchor command when raids strike at random.

sentences.zh: 」使者不能詰。

translations.literal: " The messenger could not press him further.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy had no reply.

sentences.zh: 祜寢疾，求入朝。

translations.literal: Hu fell gravely ill and asked permission to come to court.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hu grew ill and begged to visit Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 既至洛陽，會景獻宮車在殯，哀慟至篤。

translations.literal: When he reached Luoyang, it happened that the Empress Jingxian's catafalque still lay in mourning; he was grief-stricken to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: He arrived while Empress Jingxian lay in state and mourned her with devastating grief.

sentences.zh: 中詔申諭，扶疾引見，命乘輦入殿，無下拜，甚見優禮。

translations.literal: A palace edict repeatedly consoled him; leaning on illness he was led to audience; he was ordered to ride a palanquin into the hall and not bow—he received very superior courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial messages comforted him; he was carried in to audience in a litter and excused from prostrations—a rare mark of favor.

sentences.zh: 及侍坐，面陳伐吳之計。

translations.literal: When he attended audience, he stated face to face the plan to conquer Wu.
translations.idiomatic: At audience he laid out the Wu campaign in person.

sentences.zh: 帝以其病，不宜常入，遣中書令張華問其籌策。

translations.literal: The emperor, because of his illness, thought he should not enter constantly, sent Palace Secretariat Director Zhang Hua to ask his stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his health the emperor sent Zhang Hua of the secretariat to consult him instead.

sentences.zh: 祜曰：「今主上有禪代之美，而功德未著。

translations.literal: Hu said, "Now the ruling lord has the grace of orderly succession, yet merit and virtue are not yet manifest."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hu told Zhang Hua, "The throne rests on a peaceful transfer, but dazzling deeds still await."

sentences.zh: 吳人虐政已甚，可不戰而克。

translations.literal: Wu is ruled with cruelty pushed to the limit; it can be taken without a major battle.
translations.idiomatic: Wu is so misgoverned that it can fall without a hard fight.

sentences.zh: 混一六合，以興文教，則主齊堯舜，臣同稷契，為百代之盛軌。

translations.literal: Unify the six directions, raise civil culture and education—then the ruler may stand beside Yao and Shun, ministers beside Ji and Xie, setting a splendid model for a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: Unite the realm, revive rites and learning, and sovereign and minister will match the worthies of antiquity—an example for all ages.

sentences.zh: 如舍之，若孫皓不幸而沒，吳人更立令主，雖百萬之眾，長江未可而越也，將為後患乎！

translations.literal: If you set this aside, should Sun Hao by misfortune die and the Wu people set up an able lord, though you have a million men you still cannot lightly cross the Long River—it will breed trouble for later generations!
translations.idiomatic: Delay the campaign, and if Sun Hao dies and Wu crowns a competent ruler, even a million troops may never cross the Yangzi—you will leave a lasting enemy at your back.

sentences.zh: 」華深贊成其計。

translations.literal: " Zhang Hua strongly endorsed his plan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua wholeheartedly agreed.

sentences.zh: 祜謂華曰：「成吾志者，子也。

translations.literal: Hu said to Hua, "You, sir, will be the one who completes my purpose."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hu told him, "You will finish what I began."

sentences.zh: 」帝欲使祜臥護諸將，祜曰：「取吳不必須臣自行，但既平之後，當勞聖慮耳。

translations.literal: " The emperor wished to have Hu supervise the generals from his sickbed; Hu said, "Conquering Wu does not require your subject to march in person; only after it is pacified will it tax the sagely mind.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wanted him to direct operations from bed; Yang Hu said, "You need not send me to take Wu, but once Wu falls Your Majesty must govern it with care."

sentences.zh: 功名之際，臣所不敢居。

translations.literal: At the moment of fame and achievement, your subject does not dare to stand forward.
translations.idiomatic: I do not claim the glory of that victory.

sentences.zh: 若事了，當有所付授，願審擇其人。」

translations.literal: When the task is done, someone must be chosen to receive the charge—I beg you choose that man with care.
translations.idiomatic: When the war ends, appoint a worthy successor and choose him with care.

sentences.zh: 疾漸篤，乃舉杜預自代。

translations.literal: His illness grew grave; then he recommended Du Yu to succeed him.
translations.idiomatic: As his condition worsened, he nominated Du Yu as his replacement.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，時年五十八。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died, at age fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died shortly after, aged fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 帝素服哭之，甚哀。

translations.literal: The emperor wore undyed mourning and wept for him, deeply grieved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor came in white and wept for him with deep sorrow.

sentences.zh: 是日大寒，帝涕淚沾須鬢，皆為冰焉。

translations.literal: That day was bitter cold; the emperor's tears froze on his beard and temples.
translations.idiomatic: It was a freezing day, and his tears iced his whiskers.

sentences.zh: 南州人征市日聞祜喪，莫不號慟，罷市，巷哭者聲相接。

translations.literal: The people of the southern provinces, on their market day, heard of Hu's death—none failed to wail in anguish; they closed the markets, and the sound of weeping in the lanes followed one upon another.
translations.idiomatic: When southerners at the fair heard the news, they shut their stalls and filled the streets with mourning.

sentences.zh: 吳守邊將士亦為之泣。

translations.literal: Wu border troops wept for him as well.
translations.idiomatic: Even Wu's frontier soldiers shed tears for him.

sentences.zh: 其仁千所感如此。

translations.literal: Such was the reach of his humane kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the power of his benevolence.

sentences.zh: 賜以東園秘器，朝服一襲，錢三十萬，布百匹。

translations.literal: He was granted the Eastern Garden mortuary gear, one court robe, three hundred thousand cash, and one hundred bolts of cloth.
translations.idiomatic: The court gave him a state coffin set, a court dress, three hundred thousand coins, and a hundred bolts of cloth.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「征南大將軍南城侯祜，蹈德沖素，思心清遠。

translations.literal: An edict said, "General Who Conquers the South, Marquis of Nancheng Hu treads the Way in modest purity; his thoughts are lucid and far-reaching.
translations.idiomatic: The edict read: "Yang Hu, general who conquers the south and marquis of Nancheng, walked a path of plain virtue and limpid purpose."

sentences.zh: 始在內職，值登大命，乃心篤誠，左右王事，入綜機密，出統方嶽。

translations.literal: From his first posts at court, when the great mandate was received, his heart was steadfast; he aided the royal work within by mastering secrets, without by commanding the regions.
translations.idiomatic: From the founding of your reign he served at the center and on the march, guarding policy within and armies without.

sentences.zh: 當終顯烈，永輔朕躬，而奄忽殂隕，悼之傷懷。

translations.literal: He should have finished a shining career and aided Us forever—yet suddenly he is gone, and Our heart is torn with grief.
translations.idiomatic: He should have long supported the throne, yet death took him; We mourn with a wounded heart.

sentences.zh: 其追贈侍中、太傅，持節如故。」

translations.literal: Let him be posthumously appointed palace attendant and grand tutor, keeping his credential staff as before.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously name him palace attendant and grand tutor, with his old insignia restored.

sentences.zh: 祜立身清儉，被服率素，祿俸所資，皆以贍給九族，賞賜軍士，家無餘財。

translations.literal: Hu conducted himself in frugal purity; his dress was plain; whatever his salary supplied he used to support the nine agnates and reward soldiers—his house held no surplus.
translations.idiomatic: He lived simply, spent his pay on kin and troops, and left no private fortune.

sentences.zh: 遺令不得以南城侯印入柩。

translations.literal: His testament forbade placing the Nancheng marquis seal in the coffin.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered that the marquis's seal not be buried with him.

sentences.zh: 從弟琇等述祜素志，求葬于先人墓次。

translations.literal: Cousin Xiu and others recounted Hu's lifelong wish and asked burial beside the ancestral graves.
translations.idiomatic: His kinsman Yang Xiu relayed his wish to lie near the family tombs.

sentences.zh: 帝不許，賜去城十里外近陵葬地一頃，諡曰成。

translations.literal: The emperor refused, instead granting one qing of burial ground within ten li of the capital near the imperial tombs, with posthumous title Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: The throne gave him a plot by the imperial cemetery and the posthumous name "Accomplished."

sentences.zh: 祜喪既引，帝于大司馬門南臨送。

translations.literal: When the funeral cortege departed, the emperor came south of the grand marshal's gate to see him off.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor watched the procession pass from south of the grand marshal's gate.

sentences.zh: 祜甥齊王攸表祜妻不以侯斂之意，帝乃詔曰：「祜固讓歷年，志不可奪。

translations.literal: Hu's nephew, Prince of Qi Sima You, reported Hu's widow's wish not to receive marquis-level obsequies; then an edict said, "Hu declined high rank for years—his resolve could not be shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Sima You explained that Yang Hu's widow wanted a humble burial; the court answered that Yang Hu had refused honors for a lifetime.

sentences.zh: 身沒讓存，遺操益厲，此夷叔所以稱賢，季子所以全節也。

translations.literal: Though his body is gone, his yielding endures; his last principles grow only sterner—this is why Boyi and Shuqi were called worthy, and Jizi kept his integrity intact.
translations.idiomatic: His modesty outlives him, like the ancient recluses whose names honor renunciation.

sentences.zh: 今聽復本封，以彰高美。」

translations.literal: Now We restore his original fief to display his lofty virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The throne therefore restored his old patent to honor his character.

sentences.zh: 初，文帝崩，祜謂傅玄曰：「三年之喪，雖貴遂服，自天子達；

translations.literal: Earlier, when Emperor Wen died, Hu said to Fu Xuan, "The three-year mourning, though one is noble, still requires full observance—from the Son of Heaven downward.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Zhao died, Yang Hu told Fu Xuan that even emperors should keep the three-year rites.

sentences.zh: 而漢文除之，毀禮傷義，常以歎息。

translations.literal: Yet Emperor Wen of Han cut it short, injuring ritual and righteousness—I have often sighed over this.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Han had shortened mourning, to the lasting harm of propriety.

sentences.zh: 今主上天縱至孝，有曾閔之性，雖奪其服，實行喪禮。

translations.literal: Our present lord is by nature supremely filial, with the virtue of Zengzi and Min Ziqian; though court shortened his mourning garments, in substance he performs the rites.
translations.idiomatic: The current sovereign is deeply filial; though court ritual was curtailed, he still mourned in substance.

sentences.zh: 喪禮實行，除服何為邪！

translations.literal: If the rites are kept in substance, what is the point of merely removing the garments!
translations.idiomatic: When the heart keeps mourning, what good is doffing the sackcloth alone?

sentences.zh: 若因此革漢魏之薄，而興先王之法，以敦風俗，垂美百代，不亦善乎！

translations.literal: If by this we reform the shallowness of Han and Wei and revive the kings' ancient norms, thickening custom and leaving a model for ages—would it not be excellent!
translations.idiomatic: Restore ancient mourning and you reform two dynasties of slack practice and teach the realm for generations.

sentences.zh: 」玄曰：「漢文以末世淺薄，不能行國君之喪，故因而除之。

translations.literal: Xuan said, "Emperor Wen of Han, because the age was shallow, could not hold a full state mourning, so he dispensed with it.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xuan replied that Han Wendi had cut the rites because his times were chaotic.

sentences.zh: 除之數百年，一旦復古，難行也。

translations.literal: It has been gone for centuries—suddenly to revive antiquity would be hard to carry out.
translations.idiomatic: Centuries of practice cannot be overturned overnight.

sentences.zh: 」祜曰：「不能使天下如禮，且使主上遂服，不猶善乎！

translations.literal: Hu said, "If we cannot make the realm conform to ritual, at least let the ruler complete his mourning—is that not still a gain!"
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hu answered that even partial restoration—letting the emperor mourn fully—would help.

sentences.zh: 」玄曰：「主上不除而天下除，此為但有有父子，無復君臣，三綱之道虧矣。

translations.literal: Xuan said, "If the ruler keeps mourning while the realm sets it aside, you would have only father-son ties and no ruler-minister relation—the three bonds would collapse."
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xuan warned that asymmetrical mourning would break the hierarchy of loyalty.

sentences.zh: 」祜乃止。

translations.literal: Hu then dropped the subject.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hu let the matter rest.

sentences.zh: 祜所著文章及為《老子傳》並行於世。

translations.literal: Hu's essays and his commentary on the Laozi circulated in his time.
translations.idiomatic: His writings and his treatise on the Laozi were widely read.

sentences.zh: 襄陽百姓于峴山祜平生遊憩之所建碑立廟，歲時饗祭焉。

translations.literal: The people of Xiangyang, on Mount Xian where Hu had loved to rest, raised a stele and a temple, offering seasonal sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: At Mount Xian, where he had strolled and feasted, the folk built a shrine and made offerings each year.

sentences.zh: 望其碑者莫不流涕，杜預因名為墮淚碑。

translations.literal: None who read the stele failed to weep; Du Yu therefore called it the "Tear-Falling Stele."
translations.idiomatic: Travelers wept at the inscription, so Du Yu dubbed it the stele that draws tears.

sentences.zh: 荊州人為祜諱名，屋室皆以門為稱，改戶曹為辭曹焉。

translations.literal: The people of Jingzhou avoided Hu's taboo name: in speech of dwellings they used "gate" for the word, and renamed the Bureau of Households the Bureau of Declarations.
translations.idiomatic: To avoid his name they replaced one homophone character and renamed an entire bureau.

sentences.zh: 祜開府累年，謙讓不辟士，始有所命，會卒，不得除署。

translations.literal: Hu kept an opened office for years yet modestly summoned no staff; when he first issued appointments, he died before anyone could be installed.
translations.idiomatic: For years he held grand-marshal privileges yet recruited no large staff; his first four nominees arrived only after his death.

sentences.zh: 故參佐劉儈、趙寅、劉彌、孫勃等箋詣預曰：

translations.literal: Therefore adjutants Liu Jun, Zhao Yin, Liu Mi, Sun Bo, and others sent a petition to Du Yu, saying,
translations.idiomatic: His former aides wrote jointly to Du Yu:

sentences.zh: 昔以謬選，忝備官屬，各得與前征南大將軍祜參同庶事。

translations.literal: "Once, by a flawed selection, we humbly served as your subordinates and were able to assist the late general who conquered the south, Hu, in common tasks.
translations.idiomatic: "We were lucky enough to serve under the late general who conquered the south."

sentences.zh: 祜執德沖虛，操尚清遠，德高而體卑，位優而行恭。

translations.literal: Hu upheld the Way in humble emptiness; his conduct aspired to clarity and distance—high in virtue yet low in bearing, honored in rank yet reverent in deed.
translations.idiomatic: He combined lofty virtue with modest manners and honored rank with courteous conduct.

sentences.zh: 前膺顯命，來撫南夏，既有三司之儀，復加大將軍之號。

translations.literal: Earlier he received a glorious mandate and came to soothe the south; he already held the three excellencies' dignity and bore the grand general's title as well.
translations.idiomatic: He bore both ministerial rank and supreme military title in the south.

sentences.zh: 雖居其位，不行其制。

translations.literal: Though he held the title, he did not fully exercise its prerogatives.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he never exploited the full privileges of his station.

sentences.zh: 至今海內渴佇，群俊望風。

translations.literal: To this day the empire waits thirstily; worthy men still look to his example.
translations.idiomatic: The realm still looks to him with longing.

sentences.zh: 涉其門者，貪夫反廉，懦夫立志，雖夷惠之操，無以尚也。

translations.literal: Those who entered his gate—greedy men turned honest, cowards found resolve; even the integrity of Bo Yi or Liu Xia Hui could hardly surpass his.
translations.idiomatic: His presence turned the grasping toward integrity and the timid toward courage.

sentences.zh: 自鎮此境，政化被乎江漢，潛謀遠計，辟國開疆，諸所規摹，皆有軌量。

translations.literal: Since he governed this region, his rule and moral influence spread across the Jiang and Han; his secret strategies opened territory—every plan he drew had clear measure.
translations.idiomatic: His government civilized the middle Yangzi and his strategy expanded the frontier.

sentences.zh: 志存公家，以死勤事，始辟四掾，未至而隕。

translations.literal: His heart was fixed on the public good; he wore himself out in duty; he had just begun to summon four adjutants when he died before they arrived.
translations.idiomatic: He died in harness just as he began to name a staff.

sentences.zh: 夫舉賢報國，台輔之遠任也；

translations.literal: Raising worthies for the state is the high duty of chief ministers;
translations.idiomatic: To recommend talent is the first duty of the highest ministers;

sentences.zh: 搜揚側陋，亦台輔之宿心也；

translations.literal: searching talent in obscure corners is likewise their constant care;
translations.idiomatic: to seek men in humble places is their constant care;

sentences.zh: 中道而廢，亦台輔之私恨也。

translations.literal: to break off midway is their private regret as well.
translations.idiomatic: to see the work cut short is their lasting regret.

sentences.zh: 履謙積稔，晚節不遂，此遠近所以為之感痛者也。

translations.literal: He walked in humility for years; his late wish went unfulfilled—this is why far and near alike feel the pain.
translations.idiomatic: His years of modesty ended unfinished, and all who knew him grieve.

sentences.zh: 昔召伯所憩，愛流甘棠；

translations.literal: Where the Earl of Shao once rested, love still flows to the sweet pear tree;
translations.idiomatic: Men still cherish the pear tree where the Duke of Shao paused;

sentences.zh: 宣子所游，封殖其樹。

translations.literal: where Zhao Dun once walked, men planted and tended his tree.
translations.idiomatic: they tend the trees where Zhao Xuanzi strolled.
