sentences.zh: 夫思其人，尚及其樹，況生存所辟之士，便當隨例放棄者乎！

translations.literal: If men remember a person through his trees, how much more the gentlemen he summoned to office and who would now be cast aside by routine!
translations.idiomatic: If posterity honors mere trees, surely we must not abandon the aides he chose.

sentences.zh: 乞蒙列上，得依已至掾屬。

translations.literal: We beg you forward this request and let us be enrolled as staff already appointed.
translations.idiomatic: We ask the court to confirm the appointments he had begun.

sentences.zh: 預表曰：「祜雖開府而不備僚屬，引謙之至，宜見顯明。

translations.literal: Yu memorialized, saying, "Though Hu opened an office he left posts unfilled—his humility should be publicly acknowledged.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu wrote that Yang Hu's empty grand office proved his extraordinary modesty.

sentences.zh: 及扶疾辟士，未到而沒，家無胤嗣，官無命士，此方之望，隱憂載懷。

translations.literal: When, ill, he began to summon aides, he died before they came; he left no heir, and no commissioned officers—this region's hopes now carry hidden sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: He died without sons and without installed deputies, leaving the region anxious.

sentences.zh: 夫篤終追遠，人德歸厚，漢祖不惜四千戶之封，以慰趙子弟心。

translations.literal: To honor the dead and cherish the past thickens popular virtue; Han's founder did not grudge four thousand households to comfort the hearts of Zhao's sons.
translations.idiomatic: The Han founder ennobled Zhao's heirs to comfort loyal dead; we should do the like.

sentences.zh: 請議之。

translations.literal: We ask that the matter be debated."
translations.idiomatic: He asked the ministers to deliberate.

sentences.zh: 」詔不許。

translations.literal: " The edict refused.
translations.idiomatic: The throne said no.

sentences.zh: 祜卒二歲而吳平，群臣上壽，帝執爵流涕曰：「此羊太傅之功也。

translations.literal: Two years after Hu's death Wu fell; when ministers toasted the victory, the emperor raised a cup with tears, saying, "This is Grand Tutor Yang's achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later Wu surrendered; raising a cup, the emperor wept that the victory was Yang Hu's gift.

sentences.zh: 」因以克定之功，策告祜廟，仍依蕭何故事，封其夫人。

translations.literal: " He reported the conquest at Hu's shrine, following Xiao He's precedent, and enfeoffed Hu's wife.
translations.idiomatic: He announced the triumph at Yang Hu's temple and, following Xiao He's example, honored the widow.

sentences.zh: 策曰：

translations.literal: The patent read,
translations.idiomatic: The enfeoffment edict declared:

sentences.zh: 皇帝使謁者杜宏告故侍中、太傅钜平成侯祜：昔吳為不恭，負險稱號，郊境不辟，多歷年所。

translations.literal: The emperor sends Herald Du Hong to announce to the late palace attendant and grand tutor, Marquis Cheng of Juping, Hu: Long ago Wu was insolent, relied on its terrain, and styled itself emperor; the borderlands stayed closed for many years.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor tells Yang Hu's spirit that Wu had long defied the throne and blocked the frontier.

sentences.zh: 祜受任南夏，思靜其難，外揚王化，內經廟略，著德推誠，江漢歸心，舉有成資，謀有全策。

translations.literal: Hu took charge in the southern summer, sought to quiet its troubles, spread royal transformation without and planned court strategy within, showed virtue and good faith—the Jiang and Han gave him their hearts; his campaigns had resources ready, his plans a complete strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hu pacified the south, won the river country, and laid the full plan that later generals executed.

sentences.zh: 昊天不吊，所志不卒，朕用悼恨於厥心。

translations.literal: High Heaven showed no pity; his purpose was not fulfilled—We therefore mourn with bitter regret.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven took him before the work was done, and the emperor mourns that loss.

sentences.zh: 乃班命群帥，致天之討，兵不逾時，一征而滅，疇昔之規，若合符契。

translations.literal: We then ordered the commanders, executed Heaven's punishment; arms did not pass the season; one campaign destroyed Wu—his old designs matched tally and seal.
translations.idiomatic: The subsequent campaign ended Wu in a single stroke, exactly as he had foreseen.

sentences.zh: 夫賞不失勞，國有彝典，宜增啟土宇，以崇前命，而重違公高讓之素。

translations.literal: Rewards must not miss true labor—the state has its statutes; he should receive added lands to magnify the prior mandate, yet We deeply respect his lifelong habit of lofty refusal.
translations.idiomatic: The law demands reward, yet the court must also honor his lifelong refusals of fief.

sentences.zh: 今封夫人夏侯氏萬歲鄉君，食邑五千戶，又賜帛萬匹，穀萬斛。

translations.literal: Now We enfeoff Lady Xiahou as village lady of Wansui with five thousand households, and grant ten thousand bolts of silk and ten thousand hu of grain."
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xiahou becomes lady of Wansui village with five thousand households, plus silk and grain.

sentences.zh: 祜年五歲，時令乳母取所弄金環。

translations.literal: When Hu was five, he told his wet nurse to fetch a gold ring he played with.
translations.idiomatic: At five he asked his nurse for a gold ring he liked to play with.

sentences.zh: 乳母曰：「汝先無此物。

translations.literal: The wet nurse said, "You never had such a thing before."
translations.idiomatic: She said he had never owned one.

sentences.zh: 」祜即詣鄰人李氏東垣桑樹中探得之。

translations.literal: " Hu at once went to the east wall mulberry tree of neighbor Li's house and found it there.
translations.idiomatic: He led her to a mulberry by the Li family's wall and pulled the ring from the tree.

sentences.zh: 主人驚曰：「此吾亡兒所失物也，云何持去！

translations.literal: The master exclaimed in alarm, "This is what my dead son lost—how could you take it away!
translations.idiomatic: The owner cried that it was his dead son's lost toy.

sentences.zh: 」乳母具言之，李氏悲惋。

translations.literal: " The wet nurse explained in full; the Li family was moved to grief.
translations.idiomatic: The nurse explained, and the Lis wept.

sentences.zh: 時人異之，謂李氏子則祜之前身也。

translations.literal: People of the time thought it strange and said Li's son had been Hu's former incarnation.
translations.idiomatic: Onlookers said the dead boy's soul had passed into Yang Hu.

sentences.zh: 又有善相墓者，言祜祖墓所有帝王氣，若鑿之則無後，祜遂鑿之。

translations.literal: There was also a skilled tomb geomancer who said Hu's grandfather's tomb possessed imperial qi; if it were dug away there would be no posterity—Hu then had it dug.
translations.idiomatic: A geomancer warned that his grandfather's grave bore imperial omens but would cost him heirs; Yang Hu had the mound cut down anyway.

sentences.zh: 相者見曰「猶出折臂三公」，而祜竟墮馬折臂，位至公而無子。

translations.literal: The diviner, seeing this, said, "Still there will emerge a broken-armed three duke"; Hu in the end fell from a horse and broke his arm, rose to duke rank, yet had no sons.
translations.idiomatic: The seer then predicted a "three duke with a broken arm"; Yang Hu broke his arm in a fall, reached the highest rank, and died sonless.

sentences.zh: 帝以祜兄子暨為嗣，暨以父沒不得為人後。

translations.literal: The emperor made Hu's elder brother's son Ji his heir, but Ji because his father had not died could not become another's successor.
translations.idiomatic: The court first named his nephew Yang Ji heir, but Ji could not leave a living father.

sentences.zh: 帝又令暨弟伊為祜後，又不奉詔。

translations.literal: The emperor then ordered Ji's younger brother Yi to succeed Hu, but Yi likewise refused the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother Yang Yi also declined.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，並收免之。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and had both arrested and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor jailed and cashiered them both.

sentences.zh: 太康二年，以伊弟篇為钜平侯，奉祜嗣。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taikang he made Yi's younger brother Pian marquis of Juping to continue Hu's line.
translations.idiomatic: In 281 he named Yang Pian marquis of Juping to carry the line.

sentences.zh: 篇曆官清慎，有私牛於官舍產犢，及遷而留之，位至散騎常侍，早卒。

translations.literal: Pian served in office with clean caution; a private cow calved in the official quarters, and when he was transferred he left the calf behind; he rose to cavalier attendant-in-ordinary and died young.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Pian was an honest official who left a newborn calf in the public barn when he moved on; he died young as a cavalier attendant.

sentences.zh: 孝武太元中，封祜兄玄孫之子法興為钜平侯，邑五千戶。

translations.literal: In the Taiyuan era of Emperor Xiaowu, he enfeoffed Faxing, a son of Hu's great-great-grandnephew's line, as marquis of Juping with five thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaowu, a distant descendant named Faxing received the Juping title with five thousand households.

sentences.zh: 以桓玄党誅，國除。

translations.literal: Because he was executed as an adherent of Huan Xuan, the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan's faction brought his execution and the loss of the fief.

sentences.zh: 尚書祠部郎荀伯子上表訟之曰：「臣聞咎繇亡嗣，臧文以為深歎；

translations.literal: Supervisor of the Ministry of Rites Xun Bozi submitted a memorial arguing: "I have heard that when Gao Yao left no heir, Zang Wenlong deeply lamented;
translations.idiomatic: Xun Bozi wrote: "When Gao Yao died without an heir, good officials mourned;

sentences.zh: 伯氏奪邑，管仲所以稱仁。

translations.literal: when the Bo clan lost its fief, Guan Zhong was praised for benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: when the Bo family forfeited its lands, Guan Zhong was still called humane."

sentences.zh: 功高可百世不泯，濫賞無得崇朝。

translations.literal: Merit so high may not fade for a hundred generations; reckless reward cannot last a single court session.
translations.idiomatic: Great merit outlives generations; unjust grants do not survive a morning's scrutiny."

sentences.zh: 故太傅、钜平侯羊祜明德通賢，國之宗主，勳參佐命，功成平吳，而後嗣闕然，烝嘗莫寄。

translations.literal: The late grand tutor, Marquis of Juping Yang Hu, was clear in virtue and comprehensive in worth, pillar of the state, co-worker in receiving the mandate, his merit completed in pacifying Wu—yet posterity is cut off and no one tends his sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hu, chief architect of the conquest, has no descendants to tend his shrine."

sentences.zh: 漢以蕭何元功，故絕世輒繼，愚謂钜平封宜同酂國。

translations.literal: Because the Han treated Xiao He as chief founder and therefore restored his line whenever it died out, I humbly hold that the Juping enfeoffment should follow the Zan model.
translations.idiomatic: Han revived Xiao He's house; Juping deserves the same perpetual care."

sentences.zh: 故太尉廣陵公准黨翼賊倫，禍加淮南，因逆為利，竊饗大邦。

translations.literal: The late grand commandant, Duke of Guangling He Zhun, abetted the rebel Lun, brought disaster on Huainan, profited from treason, and seized a great state.
translations.idiomatic: He Zhun of Guangling aided Sima Lun's rebellion yet kept a grand princedom.

sentences.zh: 值西朝政刑失裁，中興因而不奪。

translations.literal: Western Jin's punishments then failed; the restoration therefore did not strip him.
translations.idiomatic: Western Jin let him keep it; the eastern court inherited that mistake.

sentences.zh: 今王道維新，豈可不大判臧否，謂廣陵國宜在削除。

translations.literal: Now the royal way is renewed—how can we not sharply separate right from wrong? I say the Guangling princedom ought to be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Under the renewed Jin order, that stolen fief should be struck down.

sentences.zh: 故太保衛瓘本爵菑陽縣公，既被橫害，乃進茅土，始贈蘭陵，又轉江夏。

translations.literal: The late grand guardian Wei Guan's original noble rank was duke of Ziyang county; after he suffered wrongful death his fief was advanced, first to Lanling, then shifted to Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Guan was first ennobled at Ziyang, then promoted after his murder to Lanling and Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 中朝名臣，多非理終，瓘功德無殊，而獨受偏賞，謂宜罷其郡封，復邑菑陽，則與奪有倫，善惡分矣。

translations.literal: Many mid-dynasty ministers met unjust ends; Guan's merit differed little, yet he alone received excessive reward—I say his commandery fief should be revoked and his county at Ziyang restored, so grants and revocations follow principle and good and evil are divided.
translations.idiomatic: Other loyal ministers died as he did without such windfalls; strip the extra titles and restore Ziyang to mark justice."

sentences.zh: 」竟寢不報。

translations.literal: " In the end the matter was shelved without reply.
translations.idiomatic: The court filed the petition and never answered.

sentences.zh: 祜前母，孔融女，生兄發，官至都督淮北護軍。

translations.literal: Hu's birth mother was a daughter of Kong Rong; she bore elder brother Fa, who rose to area commander who protects the army north of the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hu's natural mother was Kong Rong's daughter; his full brother Yang Fa became commander north of the Huai.

sentences.zh: 初，發與祜同母兄承俱得病，祜母度不能兩存，乃專心養發，故得濟，而承竟死。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Fa and Hu's full brother Cheng by the same mother both fell ill, Hu's mother gauged that she could not save both; then she devoted her care solely to Fa, so he was saved, while Cheng in the end died.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Fa and his brother Yang Cheng fell ill together, their mother nursed only Fa and Cheng died.

sentences.zh: 發長子倫，高陽相。

translations.literal: Fa's eldest son Lun was chancellor of Gaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fa's eldest son Yang Lun served as chancellor of Gaoyang.

sentences.zh: 倫弟暨，陽平太守。

translations.literal: Lun's younger brother Ji was grand administrator of Yangping.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Yang Ji was grand administrator of Yangping.

sentences.zh: 暨弟伊，初為車騎賈充掾，後曆平南將軍、都督江北諸軍事，鎮宛，為張昌所殺，追贈鎮南將軍。

translations.literal: Ji's younger brother Yi first was adjutant to chariot-and-cavalry general Jia Chong, later rose through general who pacifies the south and area commander of all military affairs north of the Yangzi, garrisoned Wan, was killed by Zhang Chong, and posthumously was granted general who guards the south.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yi began under Jia Chong, became general who pacifies the south, commanded the north bank from Wan, and died fighting Zhang Chong; the court posthumously named him general who guards the south.

sentences.zh: 祜伯父秘，官至京兆太守。

translations.literal: Hu's uncle by the paternal line, Mi, reached the office of grand administrator of the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hu's uncle Yang Mi rose to grand administrator of the capital area.

sentences.zh: 子祉，魏郡太守。

translations.literal: His son Zhi was grand administrator of Wei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Mi's son Yang Zhi governed Wei commandery.

sentences.zh: 秘孫亮，字長玄，有才能，多計數。

translations.literal: Mi's grandson Liang, courtesy name Changxuan, had ability and many stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Liang, style Changxuan, was clever and calculating.

sentences.zh: 與之交者，必偽盡款誠，人皆謂得其心，而殊非其實也。

translations.literal: With those who associated with him he always feigned utmost sincerity; people all thought they had won his heart, yet it was utterly not the reality.
translations.idiomatic: He feigned warm friendship until everyone thought he was sincere; almost none saw through him.

sentences.zh: 初為太傅楊駿參軍，時京兆多盜竊。

translations.literal: At first he was adjutant to grand tutor Yang Jun, when the capital region had many thefts.
translations.idiomatic: He first served Yang Jun while theft plagued the capital district.

sentences.zh: 駿欲更重其法，盜百錢加大辟，請官屬會議，亮曰：「昔楚江乙母失布，以為盜由令尹。

translations.literal: Jun wished further to tighten the law—stealing a hundred cash would add capital punishment—and called his subordinates to conference; Liang said, "Formerly in Chu, Jiang Yi's mother lost cloth and thought the theft was due to the chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jun proposed death for stealing a hundred coins; Yang Liang cited the old story of Jiang Yi's mother blaming the chief minister for her lost cloth.

sentences.zh: 公若無欲，盜宜自止，何重法為？

translations.literal: If you, my lord, have no covetousness, theft ought to stop of itself—why rely on heavier law?"
translations.idiomatic: "If superiors stay clean," he said, "thieves quit of their own accord—severity is not the cure."

sentences.zh: 」駿慚而止。

translations.literal: " Jun was ashamed and desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jun dropped the proposal.

sentences.zh: 累轉大鴻臚。

translations.literal: He rose by stages to grand herald.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Liang eventually became grand herald.

sentences.zh: 時惠帝在長安，亮與關東連謀，內不自安，奔於并州，為劉元海所害。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Hui was in Chang'an; Liang plotted with the east of the pass and, uneasy within, fled to Bingzhou, where Liu Yuanhai killed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Hui sat in Chang'an, Yang Liang conspired with the eastern lords, fled to Bingzhou, and died at Liu Yuan's hands.

sentences.zh: 亮弟陶，為徐州刺史。

translations.literal: Liang's younger brother Tao was inspector of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Yang Tao became inspector of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 杜預，字元凱，京兆杜陵人也。

translations.literal: Du Yu, courtesy name Yuankai, was a man of Duling in the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu, style Yuankai, came from Duling near the capital.

sentences.zh: 祖畿，魏尚書僕射。

translations.literal: His grandfather Ji was vice director of the masters of writing in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Du Ji had been Wei vice director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 父恕，幽州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Shu was inspector of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Du Shu had governed Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 預博學多通，明於興廢之道，常言：「德不可以企及，立功立言可庶幾也。

translations.literal: Yu was broadly learned and widely conversant, clear on the way of rise and fall; he often said, "Virtue may be beyond one's reach, yet establishing merit and establishing words may perhaps be approached."
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu read widely and liked to say that while perfect virtue might elude him, he could still hope to win fame by deeds or writings.

sentences.zh: 」初，其父與宣帝不相能，遂以幽死，故預久不得調。

translations.literal: " Earlier, his father and Emperor Xuan had not gotten along, so he died obscurely in Youzhou; therefore Yu long went without appointment.
translations.idiomatic: His father had quarreled with Sima Yi and died in disgrace at Youzhou, so Du Yu languished without office for years.

sentences.zh: 文帝嗣立，預尚帝妹高陸公主，起家拜尚書郎，襲祖爵豐樂亭侯。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen succeeded, Yu married the emperor's younger sister, the Princess of Gaolu; he first took office as gentleman of the masters of writing and inherited his grandfather's rank as marquis of Fengle precinct.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Zhao came to power, Du Yu married the princess of Gaolu, entered as a secretariat gentleman, and inherited the Fengle precinct marquisate.

sentences.zh: 在職四年，轉參相府軍事。

translations.literal: After four years in office he was transferred to join the minister of state's military staff.
translations.idiomatic: Four years later he joined the minister of state's staff.

sentences.zh: 鐘會伐蜀，以預為鎮西長史。

translations.literal: When Zhong Hui campaigned against Shu, Hui made Yu chief clerk of the west-pacifying establishment.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui made him chief clerk for the western campaign.

sentences.zh: 及會反，僚佐並遇害，唯預以智獲免，增邑千一百五十戶。

translations.literal: When Hui rebelled, his staff were all killed, but Yu alone by cleverness escaped harm; his fief was increased by one thousand one hundred fifty households.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhong Hui mutinied, Du Yu alone escaped and was rewarded with added households.

sentences.zh: 與車騎將軍賈充等定律令，既成，預為之注解，乃奏之曰：「法者，蓋繩墨之斷例，非窮理盡性之書也。

translations.literal: Together with chariot-and-cavalry general Jia Chong and others he fixed the statutes and ordinances; when finished, Yu annotated them and memorialized, saying, "Law is in general the inked line's cutting precedent, not a book that exhausts principle and exhausts nature.
translations.idiomatic: With Jia Chong he codified Jin law and wrote: "Statutes are plumb-line precedents, not treatises on metaphysics."

sentences.zh: 故文約而例直，聽省而禁簡。

translations.literal: Therefore the text is concise and the precedents straight, hearing and review are clear and prohibitions are simple.
translations.idiomatic: Good code is brief, its rules plain, easy to hear in court and simple to enforce.

sentences.zh: 例直易見，禁簡難犯。

translations.literal: When precedents are straight they are easy to see; when prohibitions are simple they are hard to violate.
translations.idiomatic: Plain rules are easy to follow; few prohibitions are hard to break.

sentences.zh: 易見則人知所避，難犯則幾于刑厝。

translations.literal: Easy to see, then people know what to avoid; hard to violate, then one nears setting punishments aside.
translations.idiomatic: Clarity keeps men from error; simplicity nearly empties the jails.

sentences.zh: 刑之本在於簡直，故必審名分。

translations.literal: The root of punishment lies in simplicity and straightness; therefore one must examine names and allotments.
translations.idiomatic: Punishment rests on clarity and fairness, which demand careful definitions of status.

sentences.zh: 審名分者，必忍小理。

translations.literal: He who examines names and allotments must endure petty refinements of doctrine.
translations.idiomatic: Defining roles forces judges to tolerate minor hair-splitting.

sentences.zh: 古之刑書，銘之鐘鼎，鑄之金石，所以遠塞異端，使無淫巧也。

translations.literal: The penal texts of antiquity were inscribed on bells and tripods, cast on metal and stone, thereby to block heterodox paths from afar and keep there from being excessive craftiness.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient laws were cast on bronze to stop clever evasion.

sentences.zh: 今所注皆綱羅法意，格之以名分。

translations.literal: What I now annotate all nets the law's intent and squares it with names and portions.
translations.idiomatic: His commentary nets the spirit of each statute and ties it to social rank.

sentences.zh: 使用之者執名例以審趣舍，伸繩墨之直，去析薪之理也。

translations.literal: It makes those who use it grasp name and precedent to judge what to take or leave, stretch the inked line's straightness, and discard the logic of splitting firewood."
translations.idiomatic: Users can match cases to named rules like a carpenter snapping a straight line."

sentences.zh: 」詔班於天下。

translations.literal: " An edict promulgated it through the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered the code published empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 泰始中，守河南尹。

translations.literal: In the Taishi era he served as acting governor of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: During Taishi he acted as governor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 預以京師王化之始，自近及遠，凡所施論，務崇大體。

translations.literal: Yu held that the capital was where kingly transformation began; from near to far, in all measures he discussed, he strove to honor the great pattern.
translations.idiomatic: He treated the capital as the model for the realm and kept policy broad-minded.

sentences.zh: 受詔為黜陟之課，其略曰：

translations.literal: He received an edict to draft a plan for promoting and demoting officials; its outline said,
translations.idiomatic: Commissioned to design official evaluations, he wrote:

sentences.zh: 臣聞上古之政，因循自然，虛己委誠，而信順之道應，神感心通，而天下之理得。

translations.literal: "Your subject has heard that high antiquity's government followed along and yielded to nature, emptied self and entrusted sincerity, and the way of trust and compliance responded; spirits moved and hearts communicated, and the patterns of all under Heaven were obtained.
translations.idiomatic: "In high antiquity rulers trusted nature, emptied themselves, and the realm fell into step without coercion."

sentences.zh: 逮至淳樸漸散，彰美顯惡，設官分職，以頒爵祿，弘宣六典，以詳考察。

translations.literal: Down to when simple honesty gradually dispersed, they displayed good and revealed evil, set up offices and divided duties, thereby to distribute noble rank and salary, broadly proclaimed the six canons, and thereby to detail investigation and assessment.
translations.idiomatic: Later ages invented offices, ranks, and the six canons to grade conduct."

sentences.zh: 然猶倚明哲之輔，建忠貞之司，使名不得越功而獨美，功不得後名而獨隱，皆疇咨博詢，敷納以言。

translations.literal: Yet they still relied on wise and clear assistants, set up bureaus of loyalty and constancy, so that names could not surpass merit and alone be praised, nor merit lag behind name and alone be hidden—all was consultation far and wide, spreading intake through words.
translations.idiomatic: Even then wise ministers cross-checked fame against real achievement."

sentences.zh: 及至末世，不能紀遠而求於密微，疑諸心而信耳目，疑耳目而信簡書。

translations.literal: Down to the final generations, unable to grasp what was distant they sought it in minute subtleties, doubted their hearts and trusted ears and eyes, doubted ears and eyes and trusted written slips.
translations.idiomatic: Decadent states mistrusted judgment and trusted paper instead."

sentences.zh: 簡書愈繁，官方愈偽，法令滋章，巧飾彌多。

translations.literal: Written slips grew ever more numerous, official conduct grew ever more false, statutes and orders multiplied, and clever ornamentation increased.
translations.idiomatic: Paperwork bred hypocrisy and ever thicker law codes."

sentences.zh: 昔漢之刺史，亦歲終奏事，不制算課，而清濁粗舉。

translations.literal: Formerly Han's regional inspectors also at year's end presented memorials; they did not fix arithmetic-style assessments, yet clear and turbid were roughly distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Han inspectors reported annually without numeric scorecards yet spotted honest and corrupt officers."

sentences.zh: 魏氏考課，即京房之遺意，其文可謂至密。

translations.literal: Wei's merit assessment followed the leftover idea of Jing Fang; its wording could be called extremely dense.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's rosters imitated Jing Fang's minute forms."

sentences.zh: 然由於累細以違其體，故歷代不能通也。

translations.literal: Yet because it piled up trivia and violated its own body, for successive dynasties it could not be applied uniformly.
translations.idiomatic: Their detail defeated their purpose and never worked cleanly."

sentences.zh: 豈若申唐堯之舊，去密就簡，則簡而易從也。

translations.literal: How could it compare to extending Tang and Yao's old ways, leaving density for simplicity—then it would be simple and easy to follow?
translations.idiomatic: Better to revive Yao-era simplicity than chase microscopic grades."

sentences.zh: 夫宣盡物理，神而明之，存乎其人。

translations.literal: To proclaim and exhaust the patterns of things, to spiritize and clarify them, rests with the person.
translations.idiomatic: Real judgment still depends on living ministers, not forms."

sentences.zh: 去人而任法，則以傷理。

translations.literal: To discard the person and rely on law will thereby injure principle.
translations.idiomatic: Law without judgment warps right principle."

sentences.zh: 今科舉優劣，莫若委任達官，各考所統。

translations.literal: Now for the examination categories' good and bad, nothing is better than entrusting eminent officials, each to assess what he oversees.
translations.idiomatic: Let senior ministers grade their own jurisdictions."

sentences.zh: 在官一年以後，每歲言優者一人為上第，劣者一人為下第，因計偕以名聞。

translations.literal: After one full year in office, each year report one superior man as highest grade and one inferior man as lowest grade, and together with the annual accounting submit the names to be heard.
translations.idiomatic: Each year each chief would nominate one best and one worst subordinate for the throne."

sentences.zh: 如此六載，主者總集采案，其六歲處優舉者超用之，六歲處劣舉者奏免之，其優多劣少者敘用之，劣多優少者左遷之。

translations.literal: Thus across six years the presiding office would gather the files: one who sat in the superior nomination all six years would be exceptionally promoted; one who sat in the inferior nomination all six years would be memorialized for dismissal; where superiors were many and inferiors few, advance him in order; where inferiors were many and superiors few, demote him to the left.
translations.idiomatic: Six years of records would decide promotion, demotion, or lateral moves."

sentences.zh: 今考課之品，所對不鈞，誠有難易。

translations.literal: Now the examination categories' pairings are not even—indeed there are hard and easy cases.
translations.idiomatic: Posts differ in difficulty, so ratings cannot be mechanically equal."

sentences.zh: 若以難取優，以易而否，主者固當准量輕重，微加降殺，不足復曲以法盡也。

translations.literal: If by a hard post one wins superior rank and by an easy one is rejected, the presiding office ought surely to weigh light and heavy and slightly raise or lower the marks—not worth bending law to cover every twist.
translations.idiomatic: The bureau must adjust scores for hard and easy assignments."

sentences.zh: 《己丑詔書》以考課難成，聽通薦例。

translations.literal: The Jimao-year edict, because examinations were hard to complete, permitted the general recommendation precedent.
translations.idiomatic: The recent Jimao edict allowed blanket recommendations when numeric grading stalled."

sentences.zh: 薦例之理，即亦取於風聲。

translations.literal: The principle of recommendation precedent likewise takes from rumor and reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Recommendations still rest on hearsay about character."

sentences.zh: 六年頓薦，黜陟無漸，又非古者三考之意也。

translations.literal: A single recommendation every six years means promotion and demotion lack gradation—again this is not the meaning of antiquity's three examinations.
translations.idiomatic: Six-year blocks without yearly steps abandon the classical three-review rhythm."

sentences.zh: 今每歲一考，則積優以成陟，累劣以取黜。

translations.literal: Now if each year there is one examination, then accumulated superiors complete promotion and piled inferiors earn dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: Annual review lets excellence compound and failure show clearly."

sentences.zh: 以士君子之心相處，未有官故六年六黜清能，六進否劣者也。

translations.literal: Considering one another with gentlemen's hearts, there has never been an officer who, across six years, six times demoted the clear and able and six times advanced the vile and inferior.
translations.idiomatic: No decent administration would yearly shame six good men and promote six knaves."

sentences.zh: 監司將亦隨而彈之。

translations.literal: The regional inspectors would also follow with impeachments.
translations.idiomatic: Censors would impeach any chief who tried it."

sentences.zh: 若令上下公相容過，此為清議大頹，亦無取於黜陟也。

translations.literal: If one ordered high and low publicly to cover one another's faults, this would be great collapse of pure criticism, and there would be no point to promotion and demotion either.
translations.idiomatic: Mutual cover would kill honest appraisal and defeat the whole system."

sentences.zh: 司隸校尉石鑒以宿憾奏預，免職。

translations.literal: Metropolitan commandant Shi Jian, from an old grudge, memorialized against Yu and had him dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jian used a private feud to cashier him.

sentences.zh: 時虜寇隴石，以預為安西軍司，給兵三百人，騎百匹。

translations.literal: At the time barbarians raided Longyou; Yu was made army director on the west-pacifying establishment with three hundred troops and one hundred mounts.
translations.idiomatic: When the frontier flared, Du Yu became staff director on the western command with a token force.

sentences.zh: 到長安，更除秦州刺史，領東羌校尉、輕車將軍、假節。

translations.literal: When he reached Chang'an, he was further appointed inspector of Qinzhou, concurrent colonel of the eastern Qiang, chariot-and-cavalry general, with credential staff.
translations.idiomatic: At Chang'an he added Qinzhou, Qiang colonel, and light chariot general with staff.

sentences.zh: 屬虜兵強盛，石鑒時為安西將軍，使預出兵擊之。

translations.literal: Because barbarian troops were strong, Shi Jian, who was then general who pacifies the west, ordered Yu to march out and strike them.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jian, commanding the west, ordered him to attack at once.

sentences.zh: 預以虜乘勝馬肥，而官軍懸乏，宜並力大運，須春進討，陳五不可、四不須。

translations.literal: Yu held that the barbarians rode victory with fat horses while government troops hung exhausted; they ought to combine strength for great transport and wait until spring to advance in punishment—he set forth five impossibilities and four needless points.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu argued the enemy was strong and Jin armies drained: mass supplies, wait for spring, and listed five reasons not to march and four wastes if they did.

sentences.zh: 鑒大怒，復奏預擅飾城門官舍，稽乏軍興，遣御史檻車征詣廷尉。

translations.literal: Jian was greatly angry and again memorialized that Yu on his own embellished city gates and official quarters, delayed and exhausted military supplies, and sent a censor with a cage cart to summon him to the commandant of justice.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jian accused him of embezzling fortifications funds and delaying logistics; a censor hauled him toward the capital in a cage cart.

sentences.zh: 以預尚主，在八議，以侯贖論，。

translations.literal: Because Yu had married a princess, he fell within the eight deliberations; judgment was by marquis-rank ransom.
translations.idiomatic: As an imperial son-in-law he qualified for the eight commutation rules and ransomed his sentence with his marquis rank.

sentences.zh: 其後隴右之事卒如預策。

translations.literal: Later events on Longyou's right wing in the end matched Yu's strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Events on the Longyou frontier proved him right.

sentences.zh: 是時朝廷皆以預明於籌略，會匈奴帥劉猛舉兵反，自并州西及河東、平陽，詔預以散侯定計省闥，俄拜度支尚書。

translations.literal: At that time the court all held Yu clear on planning and strategy; it happened that the Xiongnu chief Liu Meng raised troops in revolt from Bingzhou west through Hedong and Pingyang; an edict ordered Yu, as unattached marquis, to fix plans in the privy chamber; soon he was appointed minister of finance.
translations.idiomatic: The court valued his strategy; when Liu Meng rebelled across Bingzhou, Du Yu advised from the palace, then became minister of finance.

sentences.zh: 預乃奏立藉田，建安邊，論處軍國之要。

translations.literal: Yu then memorialized to establish the royal plow field, secure the border, and discuss the essentials of managing army and state.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed the ceremonial field, border garrisons, and fiscal-military reforms.

sentences.zh: 又作人排新器，興常平倉，定穀價，較鹽運，制課調，內以利國外以救邊者五十餘條，皆納焉。

translations.literal: He also made human-powered bellows for new implements, raised ever-normal granaries, fixed grain prices, compared salt transport, regulated tax and corvée—more than fifty items that profited the state within and saved the border without—and all were adopted.
translations.idiomatic: He patented new smelters, granaries, price controls, salt logistics, and tax rules—over fifty measures the throne accepted.

sentences.zh: 石鑒自軍還，論功不實，為預所糾，遂相仇恨，言論喧嘩，並坐免官，以侯兼本職。

translations.literal: When Shi Jian returned from the army, his merit report was untruthful; Yu impeached him, so they nursed mutual hatred, their words noisy in dispute, and both sat dismissed from office, holding marquis rank concurrent with original substantive posts.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Jian falsified battle honors, Du Yu exposed him; both were briefly stripped of ministerial titles but kept their marquisates.

sentences.zh: 數年，復拜度支尚書。

translations.literal: After several years he was again appointed minister of finance.
translations.idiomatic: He soon returned as minister of finance.

sentences.zh: 元皇后梓宮將遷于峻陽陵。

translations.literal: The late empress dowager's spirit coffin was to be moved to Junyang mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Yuan's catafalque was bound for Junyang tomb.

sentences.zh: 舊制，既葬，帝及群臣即吉。

translations.literal: By old regulation, once burial was done, the emperor and host of ministers took auspicious dress.
translations.idiomatic: Custom said court could doff mourning right after burial.

sentences.zh: 尚書奏，皇太子亦宜釋服。

translations.literal: The masters of writing memorialized that the heir apparent too ought to release mourning garments.
translations.idiomatic: The secretariat said the crown prince should likewise end mourning.

sentences.zh: 預議「皇太子宜復古典，以諒闇終制」，從之。

translations.literal: Yu argued that "the heir ought to restore antiquity and observe unplastered-chamber mourning to the end"; they followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu argued the heir must keep classical seclusion; the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 預以時曆差舛，不應晷度，奏上《二元乾度曆》，行於世。

translations.literal: Yu held that the current calendar erred and did not match the gnomon's shadow; he submitted the "Dual-Origin Qian-Du Calendar," which circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He fixed calendar drift with his Dual-Origin Qian-Du system, which went into use.

sentences.zh: 預又以孟津渡險，有覆沒之患，請建河橋于富平津。

translations.literal: Yu also held that the Meng Ford crossing was perilous and had the disaster of capsizing; he asked to build a river bridge at Fuping Ford.
translations.idiomatic: He urged a bridge at Fuping ford to end Mengjin ferry wrecks.

sentences.zh: 議者以為殷周所都，曆聖賢而不作者，必不可立故也。

translations.literal: Discussers thought that Yin and Zhou made their capitals there, yet through successive sages they did not build one—therefore it certainly could not be erected.
translations.idiomatic: Critics said sages had avoided bridging the Yellow River at the old capitals.

sentences.zh: 預曰：「『造舟為梁』，則河橋之謂也。

translations.literal: Yu said, "'They make boats into a bridge'—that speaks of a river bridge."
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu quoted the Odes: "Boats for a bridge" meant a span was possible.

sentences.zh: 」及橋成，帝從百僚臨會，舉觴屬預曰：「非君，此橋不立也。

translations.literal: " When the bridge was completed, the emperor with the hundred officials attended the gathering, raised a cup and turned to Yu, saying, "Without you, sir, this bridge would not stand."
translations.idiomatic: When it stood, the emperor toasted him before the court.

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「非陛下之明，臣亦不得施其微巧。

translations.literal: " He replied, "Without the majesty's clarity, your subject could not have applied his slight craftiness."
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu credited the emperor's support.

sentences.zh: 」周廟欹器，至漢東京猶在御坐。

translations.literal: The tilting vessel of Zhou's temple, down to Han's eastern capital, still sat by the imperial seat.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou temple's warning goblet survived until Later Han.

sentences.zh: 漢末喪亂，不復存，形制遂絕。

translations.literal: At the end of Han, turmoil and loss; it no longer survived, and its form and make were cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Warlords destroyed it and the design was lost.

sentences.zh: 預創意造成，奏上之，帝甚嘉歎焉。

translations.literal: Yu conceived the idea anew, completed it, and submitted it; the emperor greatly praised and sighed over it.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu reconstructed the goblet and impressed the throne.

sentences.zh: 咸寧四年秋，大霖雨，蝗蟲起。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xianning, autumn brought great prolonged rain and locusts rose.
translations.idiomatic: In 278 autumn floods and locusts struck.

sentences.zh: 預上疏多陳農要，事在《食貨志》。

translations.literal: Yu submitted a memorial setting forth much on agriculture's essentials—the matter is in the "Treatise on Food and Money."
translations.idiomatic: His long memorial on farming appears in the treatise on food and money.

sentences.zh: 預在內七年，損益萬機，不可勝數，朝野稱美，號曰「杜武庫」，言其無所不有也。

translations.literal: Yu was within the court seven years; gains and losses in the myriad handles of government were beyond counting; court and wilds praised him; he was styled "Du the armory," meaning there was nothing he did not have.
translations.idiomatic: Seven years at court won him the nickname "Du Armory" for seeming to stock every solution.

sentences.zh: 時帝密有滅吳之計，而朝議多違，唯預、羊祜、張華與帝意合。

translations.literal: At the time the emperor secretly held a plan to destroy Wu, yet court discussion mostly opposed; only Yu, Yang Hu, and Zhang Hua matched the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: While the court dithered on Wu, only Du Yu, Yang Hu, and Zhang Hua backed the emperor.

sentences.zh: 祜病，舉預自代，因以本官假節行平東將軍，領征南軍司。

translations.literal: When Hu fell ill, he recommended Yu to replace himself; therefore Yu with his original office and credential staff acted as general who pacifies the east and supervised the army staff of the south expedition.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hu's dying recommendation made Du Yu acting general who pacifies the east and chief of staff for the southern command.

sentences.zh: 及祜卒，拜鎮南大將軍、都督荊州諸軍事，給追鋒車，第二駙馬。

translations.literal: When Hu died, Yu was appointed general who guards the south and area commander of all military affairs in Jingzhou, granted a pursuit-swift chariot and a second pair of imperial horses.
translations.idiomatic: After Yang Hu's death Du Yu became general who guards the south in Jingzhou with pursuit chariot and double team of post horses.

sentences.zh: 預既至鎮，繕甲兵，耀威武，乃簡精銳，襲吳西陵督張政，大破之，以功增封三百六十五戶。

translations.literal: Once Yu reached his command, he repaired armor and weapons, displayed martial awe, then picked crack troops, raided Wu's Xiling superintendent Zhang Zheng, and broke him badly, for which merit his fief was increased by three hundred sixty-five households.
translations.idiomatic: He drilled the army, smashed Wu's Xiling commander Zhang Zheng, and earned three hundred sixty-five added households.

sentences.zh: 政，吳之名將也，據要害之地，恥以無備取敗，不以所喪之實告于孫皓。

translations.literal: Zheng was a famed general of Wu who held critical ground; shamed that unpreparedness brought defeat, he did not report to Sun Hao the true extent of his losses.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zheng, a Wu star, hid the scale of his defeat from Sun Hao.

sentences.zh: 預欲間吳邊將，乃表還其所獲之眾於皓。

translations.literal: Yu wished to sow suspicion between Wu's border generals; therefore he memorialized to return the captives he had taken to Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu returned prisoners to Sun Hao to make the court doubt Zhang Zheng.

sentences.zh: 皓果召政，遣武昌監劉憲代之。

translations.literal: Hao indeed summoned Zheng and sent Wuchang intendant Liu Xian to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao recalled Zhang Zheng and sent Liu Xian to Xiling.

sentences.zh: 故大軍臨至，使其將帥移易，以成傾蕩之勢。

translations.literal: Therefore when the great army arrived, it made their commanders shift and exchanged, thereby completing a momentum of toppling collapse.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of invasion Du Yu had already forced Wu to replace its best frontier general.

sentences.zh: 預處分既定，乃啟請伐吳之期。

translations.literal: Once Yu's dispositions were set, he opened a request for the date to attack Wu.
translations.idiomatic: With dispositions ready, he asked the date for the Wu campaign.

sentences.zh: 帝報待明年方欲大舉，預表陳至計曰：

translations.literal: The emperor replied that he waited until the next year to intend a great campaign; Yu memorialized setting forth the utmost plan, saying,
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wanted to wait a year; Du Yu sent a forceful counter-memorial:

sentences.zh: 自閏月以來，賊但敕嚴，下無兵上。

translations.literal: "Since the intercalary month, the bandits have only ordered strictness below, yet no troops have come up."
translations.idiomatic: "Since the leap month the enemy has barked orders but sent no reinforcements upstream."

sentences.zh: 以理勢推之，賊之窮計，力不兩完，必先護上流，勤保夏口以東，以延視息，無緣多兵西上，空其國都。

translations.literal: Pushing by pattern and circumstance, the bandits' exhausted plan cannot doubly preserve strength—they must first guard the upper reaches and diligently secure the region east of Xiakou to prolong their breathing space; they have no cause to mass troops westward and empty their capital.
translations.idiomatic: Logic says Wu must hug the upper Yangzi and eastern Xiakou, not strip the capital to reinforce upstream.

sentences.zh: 而陛下過聽，便用委棄大計，縱敵患生。

translations.literal: Yet Your Majesty has overheard and would cast away the great plan, letting the foe breed disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Delay only lets Your Majesty abandon the grand design and feed a future enemy.

sentences.zh: 此誠國之遠圖，使舉而有敗，勿舉可也。

translations.literal: This is truly the state's long-range blueprint: if you launch and fail, then not launching is acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: It is the kind of gamble statesmanship requires—if it failed, you could regret having tried.

sentences.zh: 事為之制，務從完牢。

translations.literal: Affairs need framing; strive for complete security.
translations.idiomatic: Plan for the worst and lock in every advantage first.

sentences.zh: 若或有成，則開太平之基；

translations.literal: If perchance there is success, then you open the foundation of great peace;
translations.idiomatic: Victory lays the cornerstone of lasting peace;

sentences.zh: 不成，不過費損日月之間，何惜而不一試之！

translations.literal: if not, it is no more than wasting a span of months—what is there to cherish in not making one trial!
translations.idiomatic: failure costs only a season—why shrink from one trial?

sentences.zh: 若當須後年，天時人事不得如常，臣恐其更難也。

translations.literal: If you must wait until next year, Heaven's seasons and human affairs may not be as now—I fear it will be harder still.
translations.idiomatic: Wait a year and weather, supplies, and morale may all turn worse.

sentences.zh: 陛下宿議，分命臣等隨界分進，其所禁持，東西同符，萬安之舉，未有傾敗之慮。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's long-held plan has divided orders so we advance along each sector; what each holds, east and west, matches like tallies—this is the ten-thousand-safe move, with no thought of overturning collapse.
translations.idiomatic: Your synchronized multi-prong attack is the safe, approved strategy.

sentences.zh: 臣心實了，不敢以曖昧之見自取後累。

translations.literal: Your subject's heart is truly decided; he does not dare, by murky views, invite later burdens.
translations.idiomatic: I speak plainly because I will not hide behind vague advice.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下察之。

translations.literal: Only may Your Majesty examine it.
translations.idiomatic: I beg you to weigh these points.

sentences.zh: 預旬月之中又上表曰：

translations.literal: Within a month Yu again submitted a memorial, saying,
translations.idiomatic: A month later he wrote again:

sentences.zh: 羊祜與朝臣多不同，不先博畫而密與陛下共施此計，故益令多異。

translations.literal: "Yang Hu differed from many court ministers; without first broad consultation he secretly with Your Majesty enacted this plan—therefore it all the more makes many dissent."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hu bypassed broad debate and worked the plan privately with you—that is why ministers still balk.

sentences.zh: 凡事當以利害相較，今此舉十有八九利，其一二止於無功耳。

translations.literal: In all affairs one ought to compare benefit and harm; now this move is nine-tenths benefit, and the one-tenth stops at no achievement."
translations.idiomatic: Nine chances in ten favor attack; the tenth is merely stalemate.

sentences.zh: 其言破敗之形亦不可得，直是計不出已，功不在身，各恥其前言，故守之也。

translations.literal: Their talk of shapes of defeat cannot be obtained—it is simply that plans do not come from themselves, merit does not lie on their persons, each is ashamed of his earlier words, therefore they hold to them."
translations.idiomatic: Critics fear being proved wrong and having no credit if the war succeeds.

sentences.zh: 自頃朝廷事無大小，異意鋒起，雖人心不同，亦由恃恩不慮後難，故輕相同異也。

translations.literal: From recent times, in court affairs large and small, opposing opinions have sprung like spear points; though people's hearts differ, it is also because they rely on favor and do not think of later hardship, therefore they lightly agree or differ."
translations.idiomatic: Courtiers bicker because favor blinds them to long-term risk.

sentences.zh: 昔漢宣帝議趙充國所上，事效之後，詰責諸議者，皆叩頭而謝，以塞異端也。

translations.literal: Formerly when Han Xuandi debated what Zhao Chongguo presented, after the affair's effect came, he rebuked the various debaters, who all knocked their heads and apologized, thereby to block heterodox paths."
translations.idiomatic: Xuandi silenced Zhao Chongguo's critics once facts proved them wrong.

sentences.zh: 自秋已來，討賊之形頗露。

translations.literal: From autumn onward, the shape of punishing the bandits has been rather exposed.
translations.idiomatic: Since autumn our buildup has tipped our hand.

sentences.zh: 若今中止，孫皓怖而生計，或徙都武昌，更完修江南諸城，遠其居人，城不可攻，野無所掠，積大船于夏口，則明年之計或無所及。

translations.literal: If now we stop midway, Sun Hao will be frightened and devise plans—perhaps move the capital to Wuchang, further complete and repair the southern Yangzi cities, relocate the people far off, make cities impossible to attack and the wilds nothing to plunder, and mass great ships at Xiakou—then next year's plan may miss its moment."
translations.idiomatic: Pause now and Hao can fortify Wuchang, deepen southern defenses, clear the countryside, and mass a fleet at Xiakou—then 280 may be too late.

sentences.zh: 時帝與中書令張華圍棋，而預表適至。

translations.literal: At the time the emperor was playing weiqi with palace secretariat director Zhang Hua, and Yu's memorial happened to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was playing go with Zhang Hua when Du Yu's memorial arrived.

sentences.zh: 華推枰斂手曰：「陛下聖明神武，朝野清晏，國富兵強，號令如一，吳主荒淫驕虐，誅殺賢能，當今討之，可不勞而定。

translations.literal: Hua pushed aside the board, folded his hands, and said, "Your Majesty is sagely, bright, and martial; court and wilds are pure and calm; the state is rich and troops strong; commands issue as one. The Wu ruler is dissolute, arrogant, and cruel, killing worthies and able men—now to punish him, without labor he can be settled."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua swept the stones aside and urged immediate war: Jin is strong and united, Sun Hao vile—victory will come easily.

sentences.zh: 帝乃許之。

translations.literal: The emperor then assented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 預乙太康元年正月，陳兵於江陵，遣參軍樊顯、尹林、鄧圭、襄陽太守周奇等率眾循江西上，授以節度，旬日之間，累克城邑，皆如預策焉。

translations.literal: In the first month of Taikang year 1, Yu arrayed troops at Jiangling and sent adjutants Fan Xian, Yin Lin, Deng Gui, grand administrator of Xiangyang Zhou Qi, and others to lead hosts along the river westward, handing them dispositions; within ten days they repeatedly took cities and towns, all as Yu had calculated.
translations.idiomatic: In January 280 Du Yu massed at Jiangling, sent columns upriver under Fan Xian, Yin Lin, Deng Gui, and Zhou Qi, and took town after town within ten days as planned.

sentences.zh: 又遣牙門管定、周旨、伍巢等率奇兵八百，泛舟夜渡，以襲樂鄉，多張旗幟，起火巴山，出於要害之地，以奪賊心。

translations.literal: He also sent camp-gate commanders Guan Ding, Zhou Zhi, Wu Chao, and others to lead eight hundred surprise troops, float boats in a night crossing to raid Le Township, set up many banners, and light fires on Ba Mountain, emerging at critical points to seize the bandits' hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Eight hundred commandos slipped upstream by night, feinted at Le Township with fires and flags, and seized key ground.

sentences.zh: 吳都督孫歆震恐，與伍延書曰：「北來諸軍，乃飛渡江也。

translations.literal: Wu area commander Sun Xin was shaken with terror and wrote to Wu Yan, saying, "The northern armies that have come are flying across the river."
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xin wrote Wu Yan that Jin troops seemed to fly over the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 」吳之男女降者萬餘口，旨、巢等伏兵樂鄉城外。

translations.literal: " More than ten thousand mouths of Wu men and women surrendered; Zhi, Chao, and others ambushed outside Le Township's wall.
translations.idiomatic: Over ten thousand Wu commoners surrendered while Zhou Zhi and Wu Chao lay in wait outside Le Township.

sentences.zh: 歆遣軍出拒王浚，大敗而還。

translations.literal: Xin dispatched troops out to oppose Wang Jun, was greatly defeated, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xin sallied against Wang Jun and limped back beaten.

sentences.zh: 旨等發伏兵，隨歆軍而入，歆不覺，直至帳下，虜歆而還。

translations.literal: Zhi and others raised the ambush troops, followed Xin's army inside; Xin did not notice until they reached beneath his tent, captured Xin, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The ambushers rode Sun Xin's column into camp and took him alive in his own quarters.

sentences.zh: 故軍中為之謠曰：「以計代戰一當萬。

translations.literal: Therefore the army made a rhyme of it: "Using stratagem instead of battle—one counts for ten thousand."
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers sang that Du Yu's wits did the work of ten thousand spears.

sentences.zh: 」於是進逼江陵。

translations.literal: Thereupon they advanced pressing on Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: They then closed on Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 吳督將伍延偽請降而列兵登陴，預攻克之。

translations.literal: Wu commander Wu Yan feigned requesting surrender but lined up troops on the battlements; Yu attacked and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yan pretended to yield while holding the walls; Du Yu stormed the city.

sentences.zh: 既平上流，於是沅湘以南，至於交廣，吳之州郡皆望風歸命，奉送印綬，預仗節稱詔而綏撫之。

translations.literal: Once the upper stream was pacified, then south of the Yuan and Xiang down to Jiao and Guang, Wu's commanderies all submitted at the wind's turn, presenting seals and ribbons; Yu leaned on his staff, proclaimed edicts, and soothed them.
translations.idiomatic: South of the lakes every Wu prefecture surrendered; Du Yu proclaimed amnesty under his staff.

sentences.zh: 凡所斬及生獲吳都督、監軍十四，牙門、郡守百二十餘人。

translations.literal: In all, those beheaded or captured alive included fourteen Wu area commanders and army supervisors, and over one hundred twenty camp-gate officers and grand administrators.
translations.idiomatic: He killed or captured fourteen top Wu commanders and more than one hundred twenty lesser officers.

sentences.zh: 又因兵威，徙將士屯戍之家以實江北，南郡故地各樹之長吏，荊土肅然，吳人赴者如歸矣。

translations.literal: Further, borrowing military awe, he moved garrison soldiers' families to fill the north of the river, in the old lands of Nan commandery each planted long administrators, Jing soil was orderly, and Wu people who came went as if returning home.
translations.idiomatic: He resettled garrison families north of the river, appointed magistrates in old Nan commandery, and made defectors feel at home.

sentences.zh: 王浚先列上得孫歆頭，預後生送歆，洛中以為大笑。

translations.literal: Wang Jun first in a memorial presented that he had obtained Sun Xin's head; afterward Yu sent Xin alive; Luoyang thought it a great jest.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun claimed Sun Xin's head while Du Yu shipped the living man—Luoyang laughed at the contradiction.

sentences.zh: 時眾軍會議，或曰：「百年之寇，未可盡克。

translations.literal: At the time the assembled armies debated; some said, "A hundred-year banditry cannot be fully overcome in one go.
translations.idiomatic: Some generals argued the old Wu foe could not fall in one campaign.

sentences.zh: 今向暑，水潦方降，疾疫將起，宜俟來冬，更為大舉。

translations.literal: Now we approach summer; floods will fall, epidemics will arise—we ought to wait until next winter for another great thrust."
translations.idiomatic: Summer floods and plague, they said, meant waiting until winter.

sentences.zh: 」預曰：「昔樂毅藉濟西一戰以並強齊，今兵威已振，譬如破竹，數節之後，皆迎刃而解，無復著手處也。

translations.literal: " Yu said, "Formerly Yue Yi by one battle west of the Ji took and annexed mighty Qi; now military awe is already shaken—it is like splitting bamboo: after several joints, all meet the blade and resolve, with no further place for the hand to stick."
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu cited Yue Yi and likened Wu to bamboo: once the first joints split, the rest tear free.

sentences.zh: 」遂指授群帥，徑造秣陵。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he pointed instruction to the host of commanders and went straight to Moling.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the hosts straight toward Moling.

sentences.zh: 所過城邑，莫不束手。

translations.literal: Every city passed none failed to bind hands in submission.
translations.idiomatic: City after city capitulated without a fight.

sentences.zh: 議者乃以書謝之。

translations.literal: The discussers then sent letters apologizing to him.
translations.idiomatic: The doubters wrote apologies.

sentences.zh: 孫皓既平，振旅凱入，以功進爵當陽縣侯，增邑並前九千六百戶，封子耽為亭侯，千戶，賜絹八千匹。

translations.literal: Once Sun Hao was pacified, Yu shook the troops and returned in triumph; by merit he was advanced in noble rank to marquis of Dangyang county, households increased together with earlier to nine thousand six hundred; his son Dan was enfeoffed marquis of a precinct, one thousand households; he was granted eight thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: For conquering Wu he became marquis of Dangyang with 9,600 households, ennobled his son, and took eight thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 初，攻江陵，吳人知預病癭，憚其智計，以瓠系狗頸示之，每大樹似癭，輒斫使白，題曰：「杜預頸。

translations.literal: Earlier, when attacking Jiangling, the Wu people knew Yu had a goiter on his neck and feared his stratagems; they tied gourds to dogs' necks to show him, and whenever a large tree resembled a goiter they cut it white and wrote, "Du Yu's neck."
translations.idiomatic: Defenders mocked his goiter by hanging gourds on dogs and whitewashing burls as "Du Yu's neck."

sentences.zh: 」及城平，盡捕殺之。

translations.literal: " When the city was pacified, he had them all seized and killed.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall he executed every mocker.

sentences.zh: 預既還鎮，累陳家世吏職，武非其功，請退。

translations.literal: After Yu returned to his command, he repeatedly stated that his family for generations had held civil posts, that martial achievement was not his merit, and requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to retire, claiming his lineage was civil, not military.

sentences.zh: 不許。

translations.literal: They did not permit.
translations.idiomatic: The court refused.

sentences.zh: 預以天下雖安，忘戰必危，勤于講武，修立泮宮，江漢懷德，化被萬里。

translations.literal: Yu held that though the realm was at peace, forgetting war must bring danger; he diligently practiced martial arts, built and set up the academy, the Jiang and Han cherished his virtue, and transformation spread ten thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: He kept drilling troops, built schools, and civilized the middle Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 攻破山夷，錯置屯營，分據要害之地，以固維持之勢。

translations.literal: He broke the mountain tribes, misplaced garrison camps, divided holdings of critical points, thereby to fix a posture of lasting control.
translations.idiomatic: He crushed hill bandits and dotted the frontier with forts on choke points.

sentences.zh: 又修邵信臣遺跡，激用滍淯諸水以浸原田萬餘頃，分疆刊石，使有定分，公私同利。

translations.literal: He also repaired Shao Xinchen's old works, channeled the Zhi and Yu waters to irrigate more than ten thousand qing of high fields, divided boundaries and carved stone, so that there were fixed allotments, public and private sharing profit.
translations.idiomatic: He revived Han-era irrigation, marked field boundaries in stone, and enriched both state and farmers.

sentences.zh: 眾庶賴之，號曰「杜父」。

translations.literal: The multitude relied on him and styled him "Father Du."
translations.idiomatic: People called him Father Du.

sentences.zh: 舊水道唯沔漢達江陵千數百里，北無通路。

translations.literal: Formerly the water route had only the Mian and Han reaching Jiangling for several hundred li, with no passage north.
translations.idiomatic: Only the Han connected to Jiangling; there was no northern channel.

sentences.zh: 又巴丘湖，沅湘之會，表裏山川，實為險固，荊蠻之所恃也。

translations.literal: Moreover Baqiu Lake, where the Yuan and Xiang meet, inner and outer mountains and streams are truly perilously solid—the place on which Jing's Man tribes relied.
translations.idiomatic: Baqiu, where Yuan meets Xiang, was a natural fortress for southern tribes.

sentences.zh: 預乃開楊口，起夏水達巴陵千餘里，內瀉長江之險，外通零桂之漕。

translations.literal: Yu then opened Yangkou, raised the summer waters to reach Baling for more than a thousand li, draining the Long River's peril within and opening transport to Ling and Gui without.
translations.idiomatic: He cut the Yangkou canal over a thousand li to Baoling, draining the inner Yangzi hazard and opening supply to the far south.

sentences.zh: 南土歌之曰：「後世無叛由杜翁，孰識智名與勇功。

translations.literal: The southern lands sang of him, saying, "Later ages have no revolt thanks to old Du—who can tell his fame for wisdom from his fame for courage?"
translations.idiomatic: A southern song credited later peace to Du Yu and his blend of wit and valor.

sentences.zh: 」預公家之事，知無不為。

translations.literal: " In matters of the ducal house, Yu knew nothing he did not do.
translations.idiomatic: In public business he left nothing undone.

sentences.zh: 凡所興造，必考度始終，鮮有敗事。

translations.literal: Whatever he raised and built, he always examined and measured beginning and end; rarely were there failed affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Every project he planned start to finish and rarely failed.

sentences.zh: 或譏其意碎者，預曰：「禹稷之功，期於濟世，所庶幾也。」

translations.literal: Some ridiculed his intentions as petty; Yu said, "The merit of Yu and Ji aimed at aiding the world—that is what I hope to approach."
translations.idiomatic: When called petty he answered that Yu the Great and Hou Ji also sweated small details to save the age.

sentences.zh: 預好為後世名，常言「高岸為谷，深谷為陵」，刻石為二碑，紀其勳績，一沈萬山之下，一立峴山之上，曰：「焉知此後不為陵谷乎！」

translations.literal: Yu loved to make a name for later ages; he often said, "High banks become valleys, deep valleys become hills"; he carved two stone steles recording his merit and achievement, sank one below Mount Wan, set one atop Mount Xian, saying, "How know that after this they will not become valleys or hills!"
translations.idiomatic: He set twin steles—one sunk in a river, one on Mount Xian—joking that landscapes might swap before his fame faded.

sentences.zh: 預身不跨馬，射不穿劄，而每任大事，輒居將率之列。

translations.literal: Yu personally did not straddle a horse, could not shoot through a target slip, yet whenever great affairs were entrusted, he always stood in the generals' ranks.
translations.idiomatic: He could neither ride nor shoot yet held supreme field command.

sentences.zh: 結交接物，恭而有禮，問無所隱，誨人不倦，敏於事而慎於言。

translations.literal: In forming ties and dealing with things he was respectful yet observant of ritual; in questioning he hid nothing; in teaching others he was not weary; he was keen in affairs and cautious in speech.
translations.idiomatic: He was courteous, patient, discreet in speech, and tireless in counsel.

sentences.zh: 既立功之後，從容無事，乃耽思經籍，為《春秋左氏經傳集解》。

translations.literal: After he had established merit, at ease with nothing to do, he then indulged thought in the classics and made the Collected Explanations of the Spring and Autumn Zuo Tradition.
translations.idiomatic: In retirement from campaigning he wrote the monumental Zuo commentary.

sentences.zh: 又參考眾家譜第，謂之《釋例》。

translations.literal: He also collated the various schools' genealogical tables, calling it the Explanatory Cases.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled genealogical notes as the Shili.

sentences.zh: 又作《盟會圖》、《春秋長曆》，備成一家之學，比老乃成。

translations.literal: He also made the Chart of Covenants and Assemblies and the Extended Spring and Autumn Calendar, completing a full school of learning, finished only in old age.
translations.idiomatic: He added atlas and chronology, finishing his "one school" of scholarship late in life.

sentences.zh: 又撰《女記贊》。

translations.literal: He also compiled the Appraisals on Notable Women.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote appraisals of notable women.

sentences.zh: 當時論者謂預文義質直，世人未之重，唯秘書監摯虞賞之，曰：「左丘明本為《春秋》作傳，而《左傳》遂自孤行，《釋例》本為《傳》設，而所發明何但《左傳》，故亦孤行。

translations.literal: Critics of the time said Yu's literary meaning was plain and straight, and the generation did not much esteem him; only palace library supervisor Zhi Yu prized it, saying, "Zuo Qiuming originally made a tradition for the Spring and Autumn, yet the Zuo Tradition then walked alone; the Explanatory Cases was originally set for the Tradition, yet what it clarifies is not only the Zuo Tradition—therefore it too walks alone."
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Yu alone compared his work to Zuo Qiuming's independent fame.

sentences.zh: 」時王濟解相馬，又甚愛之，而和嶠頗聚斂，預常稱「濟有馬癖，嶠有錢癖」。

translations.literal: " At the time Wang Ji understood judging horses and also greatly loved them, while He Qiao was rather acquisitive of wealth; Yu often said, "Ji has a horse obsession, Qiao has a money obsession."
translations.idiomatic: He quipped that Wang Ji loved horses and He Qiao loved cash.

sentences.zh: 武帝聞之，謂預曰：「卿有何癖？

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu heard it, he said to Yu, "What obsession do you have?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Du Yu what his obsession was.

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「臣有《左傳》癖。」

translations.literal: " He replied, "Your subject has a Zuo Tradition obsession."
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu answered, "The Zuo Tradition."

sentences.zh: 預在鎮，數餉遺洛中貴要。

translations.literal: While Yu was in command he several times sent gifts to the powerful favorites in Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: From Jingzhou he regularly sent presents to Luoyang grandees.

sentences.zh: 或問其故，預曰：「吾但恐為害，不求益也。」

translations.literal: Someone asked his reason; Yu said, "I only fear harm, not seek benefit."
translations.idiomatic: He said he paid tribute to avoid malice, not to buy favor.

sentences.zh: 預初在荊州，因宴集，醉臥齋中。

translations.literal: When Yu first was in Jingzhou, because of a banquet gathering, he got drunk and lay sleeping in the studio.
translations.idiomatic: Once in Jingzhou he drank himself to sleep in his study.

sentences.zh: 外人聞嘔吐聲，竊窺於戶，止見一大蛇垂頭而吐。

translations.literal: Outsiders heard the sound of vomiting, stole a look through the door, and only saw a great snake hanging its head and vomiting.
translations.idiomatic: Guests heard retching and peeked in to see a huge snake heaving as if sick.

sentences.zh: 聞者異之。

translations.literal: Those who heard were astonished.
translations.idiomatic: The story spread as a marvel.

sentences.zh: 其後徵為司隸校尉，加位特進，行次鄧縣而卒，時年六十三。

translations.literal: Later he was summoned as metropolitan commandant, added eminent standing, and on the journey halted at Deng county and died, aged sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled as metropolitan commandant with eminent standing, he died at Deng county aged sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 帝甚嗟悼，追贈征南大將軍、開府儀同三司，諡曰成。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly lamented, posthumously appointed him general who conquers the south and grand marshal with establishment equaling the three excellencies, posthumous name Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: The court mourned him as general who conquers the south, grand marshal, posthumously "Accomplished."

sentences.zh: 預先為遺令曰：「古不合葬，明於終始之理，同於無有也。

translations.literal: Yu beforehand wrote testament instructions, saying, "Antiquity did not join burials in one tomb—this clarifies the principle of end and beginning, same as nothingness.
translations.idiomatic: His will began: antiquity kept spouses apart in death to honor finality.

sentences.zh: 中古聖人改而合之，蓋以別合無在，更緣生以示教也。

translations.literal: Middle antiquity's sages changed it to join them—generally because apart-in-joining has no locus, they further used birth ties to display teaching."
translations.idiomatic: Later sages combined graves to teach continuity of family.

sentences.zh: 自此以來，大人君子或合或否，未能知生，安能知死，故各以己意所欲也。

translations.literal: From this on, great men and gentlemen sometimes joined, sometimes not—they could not know life, how could they know death? Therefore each followed his own intent and desire.
translations.idiomatic: Since then wise men have chosen either path, unsure of the beyond.

sentences.zh: 吾往為台郎，嘗以公事使過密縣之邢山。

translations.literal: In the past when I was a terrace gentleman, I once on official business passed Mount Xing in Mi county.
translations.idiomatic: As a young courtier he had visited Mount Xing in Mi county on duty.

sentences.zh: 山上有塚，問耕父，云是鄭大夫祭仲，或云子產之塚也，遂率從者祭而觀焉。

translations.literal: On the mountain was a tomb; I asked a ploughman, who said it was grandee Zhai Zhong of Zheng, or some said it was Zichan's tomb; then I led followers to sacrifice and inspect it.
translations.idiomatic: Locals said the mound was Zhai Zhong or Zichan; he sacrificed there.

sentences.zh: 其造塚居山之頂，四望周達，連山體南北之正而邪東北，向新鄭城，意不忘本也。

translations.literal: Its construction placed the tomb on the mountain's summit, the four views open all around; it joined the mountain body's true north-south line yet angled northeast toward Xincheng of Zheng—meaning he did not forget his roots.
translations.idiomatic: The tomb sat on the peak facing the Zheng capital obliquely—a sign of remembering one's roots.

sentences.zh: 其隧道唯塞其後而空其前，不填之，示藏無珍寶，不取於重深也。

translations.literal: Its tunnel only blocked the rear and left the front empty, not filling it, to show the store held no jewels, not taking from deep heaviness.
translations.idiomatic: The burial tunnel was left open in front to show there was no treasure.

sentences.zh: 山多美石不用，必集洧水自然之石以為塚藏，貴不勞工巧，而此石不入世用也。

translations.literal: The mountain had many fine stones yet he did not use them; he was sure to gather natural stones from the Wei River's banks for the tomb's concealment, honoring not toiling craft skill, and because such stones have no worldly use.
translations.idiomatic: He used plain river rock so grave robbers would find nothing worth stealing.

sentences.zh: 君子尚其有情，小人無利可動，曆千載無毀，儉之致也。

translations.literal: Gentlemen honor that it had feeling; petty men had no profit to move them—through a thousand years without destruction—this is what frugality achieves.
translations.idiomatic: Simplicity preserved the tomb for ages.

sentences.zh: 吾去春入朝，因郭氏喪亡，緣陪陵舊義，自表營洛陽城東首陽之南為將來兆域。

translations.literal: Last spring I entered court; because of the Guo family's bereavement, following the old meaning of accompanying the mausoleum, I myself memorialized to set east of Luoyang south of Shouyang as my future tomb domain.
translations.idiomatic: He had already bought a plot south of Shouyang east of Luoyang for his grave.

sentences.zh: 而所得地中有小山，上無舊塚。

translations.literal: Yet in the land obtained there was a small hill with no old tomb atop it.
translations.idiomatic: The plot held a bare knoll.

sentences.zh: 其高顯雖未足比邢山，然東奉二陵，西瞻宮闕，南觀伊洛，北望夷叔，曠然遠覽，情之所安也。

translations.literal: Its height and openness, though not enough to match Mount Xing, yet east attends the two mausolea, west gazes on the palace gates, south views Yi and Luo, north looks on Boyi and Shuqi—open distance in far prospect is where my feeling finds peace.
translations.idiomatic: It overlooked the eastern tombs, the palace, the rivers, and the shrines of Boyi and Shuqi.

sentences.zh: 故遂表樹開道，為一定之制，至時皆用洛水圓石，開遂道南向，儀制取法于鄭大夫，欲以儉自完耳。

translations.literal: Therefore I memorialized to mark trees and open a road, fixing a single system; at the time all will use round stones from the Luo River, open the tunnel road facing south; the rites model on the grandee of Zheng, wishing by frugality to complete myself."
translations.idiomatic: He laid out a simple tunnel southward on the Zheng model, to be built with round Luo stones.

sentences.zh: 棺器小斂之事，皆當稱此。

translations.literal: Coffin tools and minor encoffinment matters all ought to match this."
translations.idiomatic: He ordered coffin fittings to stay equally plain.

sentences.zh: 」子孫一以遵之。

translations.literal: " Sons and grandsons are wholly to obey it.
translations.idiomatic: His descendants were to obey the will to the letter.

sentences.zh: 子錫嗣。

translations.literal: His son Xi inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Du Xi succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 錫字世嘏。

translations.literal: Xi, courtesy name Shigu.
translations.idiomatic: Du Xi, style Shigu,

sentences.zh: 少有盛名，起家長沙王乂文學，累遷太子中舍人。

translations.literal: In youth he had great fame; he first rose as scholar to the Prince of Changsha, Yi, and rose by stages to palace gentleman to the heir apparent's household.
translations.idiomatic: won early fame, served Prince Sima Yi of Changsha as scholar, and became a gentleman in the heir's household.

sentences.zh: 性亮直忠烈，屢諫湣懷太子，言辭懇切，太子患之。

translations.literal: His nature was bright, straight, loyal, and ardent; he repeatedly remonstrated with Crown Prince Minhuai, his words earnest and cutting—the heir detested him.
translations.idiomatic: He bluntly lectured Crown Prince Yu, who resented him.

sentences.zh: 後置針著錫常所坐處氈中，刺之流血。

translations.literal: Later the heir set needles in the felt where Xi always sat, stabbing him so he bled.
translations.idiomatic: The prince hid needles in his seat mat and drew blood.

sentences.zh: 他日，太子問錫：「向著何事？

translations.literal: Another day the heir asked Xi, "What were you doing just now?"
translations.idiomatic: Later the heir asked what had happened.

sentences.zh: 」錫對：「醉不知。

translations.literal: " Xi replied, "I was drunk and did not know."
translations.idiomatic: Du Xi claimed drunken forgetfulness.

sentences.zh: 」太子詰之曰：「君喜責人，何自作過也。

translations.literal: " The heir pressed him, saying, "You like blaming others—why make a fault yourself?"
translations.idiomatic: The prince sneered that he loved blaming others yet feigned innocence.

sentences.zh: 」後轉衛將軍長史。

translations.literal: " Later he was transferred to senior clerk to the general who guards the army.
translations.idiomatic: He was then moved to staff the general who guards the army.

sentences.zh: 趙王倫篡位，以為治書御史。

translations.literal: When Prince Zhao of Qi usurped the throne, Xi was made supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Under Sima Lun's usurpation he became supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 孫秀求交於錫，而錫拒之，秀雖銜之，憚其名高，不敢害也。

translations.literal: Sun Xiu sought friendship with Xi, but Xi refused him; though Xiu resented it, he feared Xi's high reputation and did not dare harm him.
translations.idiomatic: The favorite Sun Xiu courted him and he snubbed the man; Sun nursed a grudge but dared not touch so famous a critic.

sentences.zh: 惠帝反政，遷吏部郎、城陽太守，不拜，仍遷尚書左丞。

translations.literal: When Emperor Hui restored rightful rule, Xi was promoted to gentleman in the ministry of personnel and grand administrator of Chengyang; he did not accept appointment, then was moved to left assistant director of the masters of writing.
translations.idiomatic: After Sima Zhong regained power, Du Xi was offered posts as personnel gentleman and Chengyang governor, declined, and became left assistant at the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 年四十八卒，贈散騎常侍。

translations.literal: At age forty-eight he died; he was posthumously granted cavalier attendant-in-ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He died at forty-eight; the court gave him the posthumous title of cavalier attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 子乂嗣，在《外戚傳》。

translations.literal: His son Yi inherited; he is treated in the "Treatise on Affines."
translations.idiomatic: His son Du Yi carried the line and has his own biography among the imperial affines.

sentences.zh: 【評贊】

translations.literal: 【Appraisal and Eulogy】
translations.idiomatic: Section heading: critical appraisal and verse eulogy.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：泰始之際，人祇呈貺，羊公起平吳之策，其見天地之心焉。

translations.literal: The history clerk says: At the threshold of Taishi, men and spirits presented their gifts; Lord Yang raised the plan to level Wu—therein may be seen the mind of Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes that in the Taishi era heaven and earth seemed to offer their mandate when Yang Hu framed the conquest of Wu.

sentences.zh: 昔齊有黔夫，燕人祭北門之鬼；

translations.literal: Formerly Qi had Qian Fu, and the people of Yan sacrificed to the ghost of the north gate;
translations.idiomatic: Qi had its Qian Fu, whom even Yan's men honored at the border;

sentences.zh: 趙有李牧，秦王罷東並之勢。

translations.literal: Zhao had Li Mu, and the king of Qin halted the momentum of annexation from the east.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao had Li Mu, who once stopped Qin's eastward roll.

sentences.zh: 桑枝不競，瓜潤空慚。

translations.literal: Mulberry branches did not compete for height; the melon's lushness left hollow shame.
translations.idiomatic: Where his virtue spread, rivalry thinned and petty envy looked vain.

sentences.zh: 垂大信于南服，傾吳人於漢渚，江衢如砥，繈袂同歸。

translations.literal: He hung great good faith over the southern domain, tipped Wu folk toward the Han shallows; the river roads lay smooth as whetstone, and swaddled sleeves turned homeward together.
translations.idiomatic: His good faith drew the south until the Yangzi ran like a highway and Wu families flocked to Jin.

sentences.zh: 而在乎成功弗居，幅巾窮巷，落落焉其有風飆者也。

translations.literal: Yet he dwelt in success yet did not cling to it, headcloth in a poor lane—how loftily he bore the gale's temper!
translations.idiomatic: He refused to clutch glory and would have retired to a scholar's scarf in a mean alley—such was his high bearing.

sentences.zh: 杜預不有生知，用之則習，振長策而攻取，兼儒風而轉戰。

translations.literal: Du Yu was not born all-knowing; once put to use he mastered practice—he flourished the long whip in attack and seizure, and combined Confucian air with turning battle lines.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu learned mastery in office: he wielded strategy in war and carried Confucian learning onto the field.

sentences.zh: 孔門稱四，則仰止其三；

translations.literal: Confucius's gate praised four attainments—then men look up and stop at three of them;
translations.idiomatic: The Master's four virtues found three mirrored in him;

sentences.zh: 《春秋》有五，而獨擅其一，不其優歟！

translations.literal: the Spring and Autumn has five aspects, yet he alone monopolized one—is that not excellence!
translations.idiomatic: among the five traditions of the Spring and Autumn he owned one entire school—rare excellence indeed.

sentences.zh: 夫三年之喪，云無貴賤。

translations.literal: Now the three-year mourning is said to know no noble or base.
translations.idiomatic: The three-year rite should know no rank;

sentences.zh: 輕纖奪於在位，可以興嗟；

translations.literal: when the light and petty wrest it from those in office, one may well sigh;
translations.idiomatic: when shallow fashion strips it from ministers, one sighs;

sentences.zh: 既葬釋于儲君，何其斯酷。

translations.literal: yet once buried it is released for the heir apparent—how cruelly harsh is that!
translations.idiomatic: to end mourning for the crown prince right after burial is cruelly abrupt.

sentences.zh: 徇以苟合，不求其正，以當代之元良，為諸侯之庶子，檀弓習於變禮者也，杜預其有焉。

translations.literal: To follow along for careless conformity, not seeking what is correct, making the age's chief heir into a feudal lord's bastard son—this is what the Tan Gong chapter rehearses in altered rites; Du Yu had a share in that.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu helped bend mourning so the heir was treated like a lesser son—just the sort of ritual twist Tan Gong warns against.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：漢池西險，吳江左回。

translations.literal: The eulogy says: The Han pool's western peril, the Wu river's leftward bend—
translations.idiomatic: The verse runs: Han's western rampart, Wu's eastern bend;

sentences.zh: 羊公恩信，百萬歸來。

translations.literal: Lord Yang's grace and trust brought a million home again.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Yang's kindness brought a million souls home to Jin.

sentences.zh: 昔之誓旅，懷經罕素。

translations.literal: Armies of old swore oaths; few carried the classics in plain cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient hosts swore fealty; few matched his blend of book and sword.

sentences.zh: 元凱文場，稱為武庫。

translations.literal: Yuankai on the field of letters was called the armory.
translations.idiomatic: Yuankai in scholarship earned the name "the armory."
